a first helm install wait never lets it run | | elitea main exits: master key invalid | not 44 base64url characters, or a trailing newline | regenerate with the Step 4 command; never echo it into a file | | elitea main exits naming the application secret key | SSO configured and elitea main sso missing or empty | create the Secret | | FATAL: sorry, too many clients already in any pod | the connection budget is wrong | set postgresql.maxConnections to the server's real value and lower main.autoscaling.maxReplicas | | Every /llm call is refused by the gateway | the two gateway identity secrets differ | put the same value in both Secrets and restart main and the gateway | | /llm answers 503 llm gateway not configured | LLM GATEWAY URL is empty | set the four LLM GATEWAY values | | Chat sends but nothing ever answers; the worker is Ready | no valid workload session, or the worker certificate's SAN differs from expectedIdentity | check the workload session Job's logs; re mint with the right WORKER ID | | Chat fails: "durable agent checkpoint store is unavailable" or a missing relation | the agent state database or its migrations are missing | create the database; set agentStateMigrations.enabled: true | | Chat fails at actor pat issuance | the account has no active personal access token | sign out and in again; one is issued at sign in | | Model picker is empty | no shared models in the public project, or aiProjectId names another project | Step 8.4; check the id | | A provider is refused although its key is right | its host is not in GATEWAY EGRESS ALLOWLIST , or it is private and only named by host | add the host, plus its IP or CIDR for a private address | | The gateway gets timeouts from elitea main | networkPolicies.main.ingressFrom does not select the gateway's data plane pods | fix the selector | | Login loops back to the sign in page | COOKIE SECURE on behind plain HTTP, or a redirect URI mismatch | serve HTTPS end to end; match the URI exactly | | Streams stop after 15 to 60 seconds | an edge request or idle timeout | Step 7, item 2 | Keeping it running Upgrades. Bump the one chart. Read the entries in docs/UPGRADING.md between your version and the new one first. The chart refuses values that a release made obsolete, so render with helm template before you upgrade. Migrations run as a hook on every upgrade. Verify what you install. Charts and images are signed with cosign: Certificate expiry. The minted runtime material is valid for 825 days by default. cert manager renews its own certificates; nothing renews the minted ones. Re mint the runtime CA, the listener, edge and worker certificates, and the elitea runtime ca Secret before they expire. Keep the master key, the PAT signing key and the database password, which the script would otherwise regenerate. Rotation costs. Rotating auth pat signing key invalidates every personal access token. Rotating application secret key signs everyone out. secrets master key cannot be rotated by replacing it. Backups. Back up both databases, the bucket, the Qdrant volume (or plan to re index) and the elitea material directory. NATS state is rebuildable: budget counters restart for the current period. GitOps. The same install as one Argo CD Application is in GitOps with ArgoCD; the chart orders NATS, its bootstrap and the platform itself with sync waves. Keep cert manager and the Issuers of Step 1 outside it, created first. Fill the Secrets from your secret manager with the chart's externalSecrets block rather than by hand; Deploy on GKE with Argo CD shows it end to end. Continue with Post install configuration and Day 2 operations. {/ source: deploy/helm/elitea/values.yaml (postgresql, dbInit, objectInit, agentStateMigrations, networkPolicies, main.env, main.runtime, llmGateway, worker, vector); deploy/helm/elitea/templates/guards.yaml; deploy/helm/elitea/values standalone.yaml; deploy/helm/elitea/values auth minimal.yaml (public origin); deploy/helm/elitea/templates/main/ingress.yaml (one / rule); deploy/gateway api/httproute.yaml; deploy/helm/elitea/values nats ha.yaml; deploy/helm/elitea/NATS.md; deploy/scripts/gen runtime certs.sh; services/elitea main/pkg/ssewriter/keepalive.go (25 second keepalive); docs/UPGRADING.md (runtime redis removed, NATS mTLS, auth document v2, Form sign in off, one chart with NATS bundled, one edge route, Helm 4). The values file on this page renders with helm template against the in repo chart. /}

title: Deploy on Google Cloud (GKE)
text: This page is the Google Cloud companion to Deploy from scratch, for chart 4.60.0 or newer . Follow that guide step by step. Where a step has a GCP specific answer, this page gives it. The goal is an install where no static cloud credential exists anywhere : object storage and the model providers authenticate as Google service accounts through GKE Workload Identity. The chart ships these answers as one example values file, values gke.yaml : Cloud SQL, keyless GCS, the GKE Ingress, Google's load balancer ranges in the NetworkPolicy, and secrets from Google Secret Manager through External Secrets, sized for about 4 vCPU and 10 GiB. Deploy on GKE with Argo CD installs it as one Argo CD Application, with every precondition and its command. | From scratch step | On GCP | | | | | Prerequisites | GKE cluster with Dataplane V2 and Workload Identity | | Step 2: PostgreSQL | Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 16+, private IP | | Step 3: Object storage | GCS bucket, Workload Identity, no Secret | | Step 7: The edge | The GKE Ingress the chart renders, or a Gateway of your own | | Step 8: Models | Vertex AI or AI DIAL with a service account, configured in the admin console | The cluster Create a GKE Standard or Autopilot cluster with: Dataplane V2 ( enable dataplane v2 ). It enforces the chart's NetworkPolicies, including ipBlock exceptions. Autopilot has it on by default. Workload Identity Federation for GKE ( workload pool= .svc.id.goog ). Every keyless path on this page depends on it. A private cluster , with Cloud NAT for egress to model providers and to ghcr.io , where the images are published. A node pool with at least one node that has 2 free CPUs for the worker during a rolling update. Optional: a GKE Sandbox node pool ( sandbox type=gvisor ) if you will turn on the cloud executor. GKE installs the gvisor RuntimeClass itself, so leave the chart's sandbox runtime installer ( sandboxRuntime.enabled ) off. See Cloud executor on Kubernetes. Install cert manager as the from scratch guide says. If NodeLocal DNSCache is on, pods resolve through 169.254.20.10 . That is a link local address, inside the deny ranges of the egress proxy and of the sandbox workspace policies, which only admit kube dns pods. Leave it off, or add the address to those policies, before you turn on the cloud executor. Service accounts Create one Google service account (GSA) per component that calls a Google API, and link it to the component's Kubernetes service account (KSA). The chart names the KSAs after the release, so with the release name elitea : | Component | KSA | GSA (example) | Needs | | | | | | | elitea main | elitea main | elitea main@ .iam.gserviceaccount.com | the GCS bucket | | elitea llm gateway | elitea llm gateway | elitea llm@ .iam.gserviceaccount.com | Vertex AI and/or the AI DIAL audience | Use linked GSAs rather than granting roles to the KSA principal directly. AI DIAL authentication needs a Google signed ID token , and GKE's metadata server issues one only for a linked GSA. Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL Create a PostgreSQL 16 or newer instance with a private IP in the cluster's VPC. No extension is needed: the platform keeps its vectors in Qdrant through elitea vector. Connections. Set the max connections database flag deliberately and copy the same number into postgresql.maxConnections . The chart checks every component's pools at their replica ceilings against it; see the connection budget. TLS. Turn on "Allow only SSL connections" and use sslmode=require in both DSNs. The chart has no mount for a server CA, so verify full is not available. No Cloud SQL Auth Proxy. The chart renders no sidecars. Connect over private IP. If your policy requires the proxy, run it as its own Deployment and Service, and point the DSNs at that Service. Cloud SQL has no superuser, so use the DBA tab of the from scratch Step 2 ( dbInit.enabled: false , dbInit.externallyManaged: true ). Create the login role with gcloud , then run the few statements below once, connected as postgres . This is the only SQL in the install. After it, the migration Job builds everything else. Set DB HOST to the instance's private IP when you run the mint script, so both DSNs point at it. GCS bucket with no keys elitea main needs more than object access on its bucket. At boot it replaces the bucket's lifecycle configuration ( storage.buckets.update ) and reads its encryption settings. roles/storage.admin granted on the bucket alone covers both. Use a dedicated bucket. In the values file, replace the S3 block of the from scratch Step 6 with: Also remove S3 ACCESS KEY and S3 SECRET KEY from main.secrets , and do not create elitea main storage secrets . With Application Default Credentials there is no signing key, so the platform does not hand out presigned URLs: downloads and workspace transfers stream through elitea main instead. Nothing needs configuring for that. With no Secret and no annotation, the Google client library falls back to the node's own service account. If that account can reach the bucket, elitea main starts and works under the wrong identity. Always set the annotation. The edge The public edge is one route, / to elitea main:8080 : elitea main relays /app and /docs to elitea web, serves its MCP endpoint itself, and deletes client supplied identity headers before any route runs. From scratch Step 7 lists what the edge must still do: keep server sent event streams open for minutes and accept 150 MiB uploads. The chart renders it: the standard Google Cloud external Application Load Balancer, with container native load balancing straight to the elitea main pods. main.ingress.gke adds a BackendConfig ( timeoutSec: 3600 , so a streamed answer outlives the load balancer's 30 second default; an HTTP health check on /healthz port 8080; connection draining; the optional Cloud Armor policy) and a FrontendConfig (HTTP to HTTPS redirect, the optional SSL policy). main.ingress.certManager has cert manager issue the tls Secret the load balancer serves. Add Google's ranges to ELITEA TRUSTED PROXY CIDRS too. Behind a CDN or proxy, issue the origin certificate through that provider's cert manager issuer ( certManager.issuerKind , issuerGroup ) and attach a Cloud Armor policy that admits only the proxy's ranges; Deploy on GKE with Argo CD has the commands. elitea main writes a comment into every idle stream after 25 seconds, inside a proxy's idle timeout of about 100 seconds. Any Gateway API implementation works with the one route, the managed GKE Gateway ( gke l7 global external managed ) included: render it with main.ingress.gatewayApi: true , or apply deploy/gateway api/httproute.yaml . The managed GKE Gateway has the same 30 second backend default: attach a GCPBackendPolicy to the elitea main Service with timeoutSec of, for example, 3600, and a HealthCheckPolicy on /healthz port 8080. It has no gateway pods, so networkPolicies.main.ingressFrom is the two ipBlock s above. Envoy Gateway in the cluster, exposed by a Service of type LoadBalancer : select its data plane pods in ingressFrom ( app.kubernetes.io/name: envoy in envoy gateway system ). Run every check of the from scratch Step 9 before go live. Single sign on Install with OIDC configured in the values file ( OIDC in from scratch Step 6). That is what makes the sign in routes exist. Any identity provider with OIDC works, including Google Workspace ( OIDC ISSUER URL: https://accounts.google.com ), Entra ID, Okta and Keycloak. Name the first administrator as email: . That form matches when the provider marks the address as verified. After the first sign in, everything else is in the admin console, under Configuration › Authentication , with no restart: SAML. Add a SAML 2.0 provider. Give the identity provider this service's metadata URL, https:// /auth/saml/metadata , and copy its entity ID, SSO URL and certificate back into the form. Signing authentication requests is optional. SCIM. Create a SCIM client, put its Tenant URL and token into the identity provider, then bind directory groups to a project and a role. Authentication describes every field. Platform models with a service account Platform models are the shared models every project can use. An administrator adds them in the admin console. On GCP, authenticate them as the gateway's service account rather than with a pasted key. 1. Allow workload identity on the gateway It needs chart 4.60.0 or newer . Older charts have no llmGateway.workloadIdentity and render no annotations on the gateway's service account. Workload identity is off by default, and it is honoured only for platform credentials, the ones an administrator adds in the admin console. A project's own credential can never borrow the gateway's identity. A private AI DIAL address needs its IP or CIDR in the allowlist as well; see model egress. 2. Grant the service account access Enable the Vertex AI API in that project. To use models from another project, grant the role there and enter that project in the provider form. The gateway signs in to DIAL with a Google signed ID token for elitea llm@ .iam.gserviceaccount.com , sent as Authorization: Bearer . The token's audience is the DIAL endpoint's origin, unless you set another one in the provider form. Your DIAL administrators configure DIAL core to accept that token: an identity provider with issuer https://accounts.google.com and JWKS https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs accept only the audience above and this service account's e mail (or sub ) give that principal a role with access to the models you will publish Until that is in place, the connection check in the admin console fails with DIAL's 401 . 3. Add the provider and publish models In the admin console, open Configuration › LLM Proxy › Providers & models . Choose Vertex AI or EPAM DIAL , and set Authentication to Workload identity (GKE service account) . Vertex AI: the Google Cloud project and location. There is no key field. EPAM DIAL: the endpoint and API version, plus a token audience if your DIAL expects one other than the endpoint's origin. Save the provider, then run Test connection . A keyless provider can be tested only after it is saved. A warning under the Workload identity option means llmGateway.workloadIdentity.enabled is not on. Add a platform model for each model you share: its name as the provider knows it, its context window, and, for DIAL, its DIAL protocol . Default fits most models. Choose OpenAI Responses API for gpt models that need it, and Anthropic Messages API for Claude with extended thinking. Set it on the same tab. New conversations use it. Then open a chat as any user, pick a shared model and send a message. Checklist for the values file On top of the from scratch values file (the chart's values gke.yaml has all of this, plus the edge and externalSecrets ): {/ source: deploy/helm/elitea/values.yaml (main.env GCS ENDPOINT, main.serviceAccount, llmGateway.serviceAccount, llmGateway.workloadIdentity, sandboxKubernetes.runtimeClass); deploy/helm/elitea/env drift allowlist.txt (GOOGLE APPLICATION CREDENTIALS not wired); services/elitea main/internal/infra/storage/gcs/backend.go (ADC, no presign, lifecycle); services/elitea llm gateway/internal/account (workload identity for platform credentials); deploy/helm/elitea sandbox runtime/README.md (not needed on GKE); deploy/helm/elitea/values gke.yaml; deploy/helm/elitea/values.yaml (main.ingress.gke, main.ingress.certManager, sandboxRuntime); deploy/helm/tests/render gke ingress.sh; docs/UPGRADING.md (GKE Ingress support and SSE keepalives, one edge route). GKE Gateway policies are GKE product behaviour, not tested by this repository: verify against Google's GKE Gateway documentation for your GKE version. /}

title: Deploy on GKE with Argo CD
text: This page installs Elitea on Google Kubernetes Engine from one Argo CD Application that syncs one chart , oci://ghcr.io/elitea ng/charts/elitea . The chart carries everything that runs in the cluster: the platform, NATS JetStream and its stream bootstrap, the vector store (elitea vector and the bundled Qdrant), DeepWiki, Inventory and the GKE edge objects. Each feature is on by default and is one switch ( .enabled: false leaves it out). No static cloud credential exists anywhere: object storage and the model providers authenticate as Google service accounts, and every secret comes from Google Secret Manager. It is the GitOps path through the same install as Deploy from scratch and Deploy on Google Cloud (GKE). Those pages explain each choice; this one lists what must exist, the commands that create it, and the order of the first sync. The examples it refers to are in deploy/argocd/examples/gke/ , written to be copied into a GitOps repository your organisation owns. NATS, its certificates and the bootstrap Job are part of the elitea release, and so is Qdrant (the upstream qdrant chart, StatefulSet elitea vectordb ); there are no separate nats , nats bootstrap or Qdrant charts to install. The sandbox runtime installer is a dependency of the same chart ( sandboxRuntime.enabled ), but GKE does not need it: a GKE Sandbox node pool ships the gvisor RuntimeClass. Leave it off. Coming from the three Application layout? Follow "One chart: NATS bundled" in docs/UPGRADING.md first. Preconditions The chart creates none of these. Each one fails the first sync, or a pod soon after it, when it is missing. | Precondition | What it must be | Commands | | | | | | GKE cluster | Dataplane V2, Workload Identity Federation, private nodes, Cloud NAT | The cluster | | cert manager | installed, with the elitea internal ca and elitea runtime ca Issuers in the elitea namespace | cert manager | | Cloud SQL | PostgreSQL 16+, private IP, "Allow only SSL connections", role and two databases created by hand | Cloud SQL | | GCS bucket and service accounts | a dedicated bucket, the elitea main service account with roles/storage.admin on that bucket only | GCS and service accounts | | DNS and TLS | a global static IP, a DNS record for it, a cert manager issuer for the public certificate | Edge | | External Secrets Operator | installed, with a ClusterSecretStore on Secret Manager | Secrets | | Argo CD | installed, with the chart registry registered | Argo CD | | KEDA | installed once for the cluster (or keda.enabled: true in a cluster that has none) | Autoscaling | | Capacity | about 4 vCPU and 10 GiB of requests for the release | Budget | The commands use these names. Change them consistently: The cluster Create a GKE Standard or Autopilot cluster with Dataplane V2 ( enable dataplane v2 ; it enforces the chart's NetworkPolicies, ipBlock included), Workload Identity Federation ( workload pool=$PROJECT ID.svc.id.goog ) and private nodes . Give the private nodes egress through Cloud NAT, for ghcr.io , where the images are published, and for the model providers: The cluster on the Google Cloud page has the node sizing and the NodeLocal DNSCache caveat. cert manager Install cert manager cluster wide. The NATS CA, every NATS identity, the LLM gateway's, DeepWiki's and Inventory's mTLS hops, elitea vector, Qdrant's TLS and the providers' callback client certificates are cert manager Certificate s; you mint none of them by hand. Then create the namespace and the two Issuers the values name, exactly as in Deploy from scratch, Step 1: elitea internal ca : self signed by cert manager; nothing leaves the cluster. It issues the gateway, DeepWiki and Inventory hops. elitea runtime ca : a CA Issuer backed by the Secret elitea runtime ca . It issues elitea vector's pair, Qdrant's elitea qdrant tls and the elitea deepwiki callback client / elitea inventory callback client certificates. On this path that Secret comes from Secret Manager (below), so the Issuer turns Ready on the first sync. The NATS CA is the chart's own ( elitea nats ca , wave 10 ); you create nothing for it. A cert manager Cluster Issuer for the public certificate (ACME, or the origin CA issuer of a proxy in front) is the third thing cert manager needs; see Edge. Cloud SQL Create a PostgreSQL 16 or newer instance with a private IP on the cluster's VPC (private services access) and "Allow only SSL connections" : values gke.yaml sizes for this tier: 4 vCPU and 16 GB, where Cloud SQL sets max connections to 500 from the memory size ( postgresql.maxConnections: 500 ). The chart adds up every component at its replica ceiling (elitea main, the gateway, the scheduler, DeepWiki, Inventory and the worker's agent state: 359) and refuses a release that does not fit in 500 minus the 25 it reserves. If you set database flags max connections=… yourself, state the same number in postgresql.maxConnections . Scaling has the formula. Cloud SQL has no superuser, so prepare the role and both databases once by hand. The password is the db password that the mint script in the first of the steps writes: Then, connected as postgres : values gke.yaml keeps the chart's database preparation hook off and says the databases exist ( dbInit.enabled: false , dbInit.externallyManaged: true ). Every DSN carries ?sslmode=require : the connection is encrypted, and the server certificate is not verified. verify ca and verify full are not supported yet, because the chart mounts no server CA. There is no Cloud SQL Auth Proxy. GCS and service accounts The bucket and the Google service account are yours to create; the chart never creates a GCS bucket ( objectInit stays off): roles/storage.objectAdmin alone is not enough: elitea main rewrites the bucket's lifecycle rule at every start ( storage.buckets.update ) and exits when it cannot, so it crash loops. roles/storage.admin bound on the bucket covers it; so does objectAdmin plus a custom role with storage.buckets.get and storage.buckets.update . Optional: Vertex AI without a key. The LLM gateway can call Vertex AI as its own service account for platform credentials ( llmGateway.workloadIdentity , on in values gke.yaml ): Platform models with a service account covers AI DIAL and the admin console side. Edge: IP, DNS, TLS and an optional proxy The chart's GKE Ingress is one / rule to elitea main . elitea main serves the API, redirects / to /app/ , relays /app and /docs to elitea web, and serves the MCP endpoint ( /app/ /mcp ) itself, so no path rule, regular expression or header filter is needed at the load balancer. elitea main deletes client supplied identity headers itself. With main.ingress.gke on, the chart renders, next to the Ingress: a BackendConfig : timeoutSec: 3600 , so a streamed answer is not cut at the load balancer's 30 second default; an HTTP health check on /healthz port 8080; connection draining; and an optional Cloud Armor securityPolicy ; a FrontendConfig : HTTP to HTTPS redirect, and an optional sslPolicy ; the cloud.google.com/neg annotation on the elitea main Service, so Google's front ends reach the pods directly. There are no ingress pods, so networkPolicies.main.ingressFrom must admit Google's ranges 35.191.0.0/16 and 130.211.0.0/22 ; values gke.yaml does. main.ingress.certManager.clusterIssuer annotates the Ingress, and cert manager issues the tls[].secretName Secret that the load balancer serves. Server sent event streams carry a comment after 25 seconds of silence, well inside an idle timeout of about 100 seconds at a proxy in front. Behind a CDN or proxy (Cloudflare or similar): issue the origin certificate through that provider's cert manager issuer ( main.ingress.certManager.issuerKind and issuerGroup name an external issuer), and keep everyone else off the load balancer with a Cloud Armor policy that admits only the proxy's published ranges: A rule takes a limited number of ranges, so split a long list across several rules. Then set main.ingress.gke.backendConfig.securityPolicy: elitea proxy only . Add the proxy's ranges to ELITEA TRUSTED PROXY CIDRS only if elitea main should take the client address from the proxy's forwarding header. External Secrets Operator Install the External Secrets Operator (ESO) and give it a ClusterSecretStore on Secret Manager. The example store, bootstrap/cluster secret store.yaml , has no auth block: ESO's controller authenticates as its own Kubernetes service account through Workload Identity. The file's header has the gcloud commands that create that service account, grant it roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor on the two secrets below only, and link it. Then: With externalSecrets.enabled , the chart renders one external secrets.io/v1 ExternalSecret for every Secret it consumes , derived from the same values the workloads read, so the list cannot drift from the pods. They are PreSync hooks in wave 30 , so the Secrets exist before the migration Jobs that read them. Plain Kubernetes Secrets ( existingSecret and friends) still work, but are not recommended in production. Argo CD Argo CD pulls the chart from ghcr.io as an OCI Helm chart. Register the registry once; the charts are public, so the entry carries no credential: Argo CD renders the chart with the Helm 3 it bundles, and the chart supports that (Helm 3.8 or newer). The Argo CD project you deploy into must allow the elitea namespace as a destination. The OCI chart carries its dependencies (the upstream NATS, Qdrant, KEDA and prometheus adapter charts included), so the project needs no other source repository. A git source also needs https://nats io.github.io/k8s/helm/charts/ , https://qdrant.github.io/qdrant helm , https://kedacore.github.io/charts and https://prometheus community.github.io/helm charts in sourceRepos (see GitOps with Argo CD). In an air gapped cluster, mirror the OCI chart: it carries all four. Autoscaling values gke.yaml turns autoscaling on: the worker scales on its JetStream backlog (1 to 4), DeepWiki on its running invocations (1 to 3, KEDA's postgresql trigger on the host's own Cloud SQL Secret), the gateway on CPU (1 to 3) and elitea main on CPU (2 to 3). The worker and DeepWiki need KEDA , and there are two ways to provide it: KEDA installed once for the cluster (the default here). KEDA is cluster infrastructure: it outlives this release, and deleting the release then never takes the CRDs, or other teams' ScaledObjects, with it. Install it before the first sync. values gke.yaml sets scaling.keda.clusterInstalled: true , which tells the chart about it, because Argo CD does not pass the cluster's API versions. KEDA in this release. Set keda.enabled: true and scaling.keda.clusterInstalled: false , only in a cluster with no KEDA: it is one per cluster. Add KEDA's three pods to the resource budget. On the first sync the ScaledObjects come after the CRDs (each carries SkipDryRunOnMissingResource=true ). With a Prometheus in the cluster, set scaling.prometheus.serverAddress and both the gateway and DeepWiki move to their Prometheus triggers, on concurrent /llm streams and on running invocations. Scaling has what each component scales on, the disruption budgets and the grace periods. Resource budget values gke.yaml is sized for 4 vCPU and 10 GiB of requests with every default on (DeepWiki and Inventory included), at steady state and at the peak of any one rollout. CI sums the rendered requests, adds the largest rollout surge, and fails a change that breaks either. | State | CPU requests | Memory requests | | | | | | Steady state | 3670m | 8704Mi | | Peak during a rollout (the largest single surge) | 3920m | 9856Mi | The worker is the largest pod (1.5 vCPU, 3 GiB). It does not surge: values gke.yaml sets worker.rollingUpdate and main.rollingUpdate to maxSurge: 0, maxUnavailable: 1 . The old pod stops before the new one starts. Commands wait in JetStream for the minute the new worker takes to start, and one of the two elitea main replicas keeps serving. With a surging worker the peak would be 5.2 vCPU / 11.5 GiB. Hook Jobs run for seconds and are not counted. At elitea main's autoscaler maximum of 3, the steady state is 4070m / 9472Mi; scaling out under load uses the cluster's headroom above the reservation. To win back 450m / 1.5 GiB, leave DeepWiki or Inventory off ( enabled: false ). Qdrant also needs a 50Gi PersistentVolumeClaim ( standard rwo ). Steps Run the mint script of Deploy from scratch, Step 4 with DB HOST set to the Cloud SQL private IP. It writes every generated value into ./elitea material , and both DSNs with sslmode=require . A Secret Manager property is a JSON string, so two keys the script writes as raw bytes are rewritten as text of a length the platform accepts. Add the gateway's hop detection secret, then build one JSON object whose property names are the Kubernetes Secret and the key joined by / , for example elitea main sso/oidc client secret : That is the whole inventory for the install on this page, every default on: 29 properties in elitea platform , and the platform DSN alone in elitea database url , so a password rotation touches one secret. The elitea runtime ca pair is listed by the example values as an extra Secret, because no pod reads it; the elitea runtime ca Issuer does. Turning on an optional component (the cloud executor, say) adds Secrets, and turning a default off ( deepwiki.enabled: false ) removes its own; render the chart with your values and read the ExternalSecrets for the exact property list: A missing property holds back its whole Kubernetes Secret: ESO syncs all keys of an ExternalSecret or none. Keep elitea material out of git and somewhere safe; losing secrets master key makes every stored credential unreadable. Start from the chart's own values gke.yaml and override only what is yours. The example Application, applications/elitea.yaml , does exactly that: valueFiles: [values gke.yaml] (the file ships inside the published chart) and a short values block with the store name, the hostnames, the Google service accounts, the bucket, the OIDC client and the gateway origins. Pin targetRevision to an exact chart version. Read values gke.yaml once in full: it states the Cloud SQL, GCS, Ingress, NetworkPolicy, NATS and Qdrant settings this page relies on. It lets DeepWiki and Inventory clone from github.com only; restate deepwiki.env.ELITEA DEEPWIKI GIT ALLOWLIST and inventory.env.ELITEA INVENTORY GIT ALLOWLIST for your git hosts (the chart copies each to elitea main). For three Qdrant nodes, add the chart's values qdrant ha.yaml . Render your values before git does it for you. Each refusal names the field: For three NATS nodes, add the chart's values nats ha.yaml after values gke.yaml ; it raises the bootstrap's replica count with it. Copy deploy/argocd/examples/gke/ into your GitOps repository, point root.yaml at it, and apply the root once: It renders applications/ , which holds one Application, elitea . bootstrap/ is not rendered by the root: you applied it by hand above. Everything happens inside the one elitea Application, in this order: | Phase | What runs | | | | | PreSync , wave 30 | the ExternalSecrets; Argo CD waits until each is Ready | | PreSync | the platform and agent state migrations; a failed migration stops the sync | | PreSync , wave 10 | the workload session Job (the worker's row in elitea runtime.workload sessions ) | | wave 10 | the NATS server, its CA, server and client certificates, and the elitea nats bootstrap Job, a Sync hook that creates every stream and KV bucket | | wave 5 | elitea vector and Qdrant (the bundled qdrant chart) with its TLS Certificate | | wave 0 | elitea main, elitea web, the scheduler, the LLM gateway, DeepWiki, Inventory, the OTel collector, the Ingress, BackendConfig and FrontendConfig | | wave 1 | the agent worker | The Google load balancer takes several minutes to program after the Ingress appears, and the certificate is issued once DNS points at the static IP. With the Helm CLI instead of Argo CD, the same chart installs with helm install elitea oci://ghcr.io/elitea ng/charts/elitea version n elitea f values gke.yaml f your values.yaml . Do not pass wait on a first install: the bootstrap Job is a post install hook, and the workloads wait for the streams it creates. Helm 4.3 or newer is recommended for the CLI; Helm 3.8 or newer also works. Argo CD deletes the bootstrap Job when it succeeds, so argocd app get is where its result shows; a Job still in the namespace is one that failed, and its log names the stream or account. Then sign in, add a model provider and send a chat message, as in Deploy from scratch, Step 8. Troubleshooting | Symptom | Likely cause | Fix | | | | | | The Ingress has no address, or the backend is UNHEALTHY | the load balancer's health checks are refused by the NetworkPolicy | networkPolicies.main.ingressFrom must hold 35.191.0.0/16 and 130.211.0.0/22 | | Streams stop with a 502 after about 30 seconds | the BackendConfig is not attached, so the backend keeps the 30 second default | check main.ingress.gke.enabled (or className: gce ), the cloud.google.com/backend config annotation on the Service and timeoutSec: 3600 | | Every request returns 403 from Google | the Cloud Armor policy does not admit the caller | add the proxy's current ranges, or clear securityPolicy while you test | | The sync waits on an ExternalSecret that never turns Ready | the store, or ESO's identity, cannot read the secret, or a property is missing | kubectl n elitea describe externalsecret ; check the store's READY, ESO's roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor and its Workload Identity link; compare the properties with the render | | elitea main CrashLoopBackOff right after a green sync, naming the bucket | the service account cannot update the bucket's lifecycle rule | grant roles/storage.admin on the bucket (not only objectAdmin ) | | elitea main reads the bucket as the node's identity, or is refused | the iam.gke.io/gcp service account annotation or the workloadIdentityUser binding is missing | set both for $NS/elitea main | | Migrations fail with an SSL or pg hba error | the DSN has no sslmode , or verify ca / verify full | use sslmode=require in both DSNs | | Migrations fail with permission denied to create database or a missing database | the databases were not prepared by hand | run the three SQL statements of Cloud SQL | | FATAL: sorry, too many clients already | postgresql.maxConnections is above the instance's flag | set both to the same number; lower main.autoscaling.maxReplicas | | The bootstrap Job or the NATS pod stays Pending on a Secret | cert manager has not issued the NATS certificates | kubectl n elitea get certificates,certificaterequests ; cert manager must be running before the sync | | elitea vector waits for its certificate | the elitea runtime ca Issuer is not Ready | its Secret comes from the elitea runtime ca ExternalSecret; check that one first | | The public certificate is never issued | DNS does not point at the static IP yet, or the issuer named in certManager does not exist | kubectl n elitea describe certificate elitea tls | | elitea main exits naming NATS or the presence bucket | the bootstrap Job has not succeeded | argocd app get elitea , then the Job's log | | Vertex AI calls fail with a permission error | the gateway's service account lacks roles/aiplatform.user , or llmGateway.workloadIdentity is off | grant the role; keep the annotation and the switch | Deploy from scratch has the symptoms that are not specific to Google Cloud. GitOps with ArgoCD covers promotion and rollback. {/ source: deploy/argocd/examples/gke/ (root.yaml, applications/elitea.yaml, bootstrap/); deploy/helm/elitea/values gke.yaml (preconditions, budget, externalSecrets, postgresql, dbInit, objectInit, networkPolicies.main.ingressFrom, main.ingress.gke, llmGateway.workloadIdentity, sandboxRuntime); deploy/helm/elitea/values.yaml (externalSecrets modes and ordering, main.ingress certManager and gke, sandboxRuntime); deploy/helm/tests/render external secrets.sh, render gke ingress.sh, render gke budget.sh; deploy/helm/elitea/templates/externalSecrets/; services/elitea main/pkg/ssewriter/keepalive.go (25 second keepalive); services/elitea main/internal/authcomposition/config.go (attempt key 32 to 64 bytes); services/elitea worker rust/src/spool.rs (32 byte spool key); docs/UPGRADING.md (one chart, one edge route, GKE Ingress, Helm 4). The property list is the render of values gke.yaml plus the example values. Google Cloud commands are product behaviour, not tested by this repository. /}

title: Install with Helm
text: This walks a Kubernetes install of the elitea chart end to end. It is one chart for everything: the platform, NATS JetStream with its stream bootstrap, the vector store and, where a cluster needs it, the sandbox runtime installer. Read Production deployment overview first for the topology and what the chart does not provision. For a first install on an empty cluster, Deploy from scratch has every Secret, certificate authority, database step and edge rule in one place, with a complete values file. Prerequisites A Kubernetes cluster with kubectl and helm configured against it. Helm 4.3 or newer is recommended; Helm 3.8 or newer also renders the chart, which is what Argo CD uses. With Helm 4, atomic is rollback on failure . Reachable, with an administrator DSN available for the database preparation Job ( CREATE DATABASE ). No extension is needed: vectors are kept in Qdrant through elitea vector ( vector.enabled ), not in PostgreSQL. Bundled: the chart runs it ( nats.enabled , on by default) and creates its streams with a hook Job ( natsBootstrap ). The platform needs no Redis: the runtime command bus, live updates and presence are on NATS, and the chart refuses values that still set runtimeRedis . An S3 compatible bucket, created ahead of the first sync and named by main.env.STORAGE CONTAINER . Required. The bundled NATS CA, the NATS client identities and the LLM gateway's mTLS hop (on by default) are all cert manager Certificate s. The gateway's issuer ( llmGateway.mtls.issuerRef , default ClusterIssuer elitea internal ca ) is yours to create. Secrets to create beforehand Nothing secret goes in a values file — a Helm parameter renders into a ConfigMap, readable by anyone with get on the namespace. Create these Kubernetes Secrets first; the chart only ever takes their names . Wraps each project's vault key. Required by both elitea main and the gateway, and it must be the same key: elitea main reads the gateway's reference ( llmGateway.secrets.SECRETS MASTER KEY , default Secret elitea llm gateway secrets , key secrets master key ) unless you override both. Generate: python3 c 'import base64, os; print(base64.urlsafe b64encode(os.urandom(32)).decode())' The database DSN, one Secret + key pair that every component reading the database (elitea main, its migration Job, the scheduler, the LLM gateway, the workload session Job) derives its DATABASE URL from. Default names: Secret elitea main db , key database url . Agent execution signing keys and listener certificates (from deploy/scripts/gen runtime certs.sh ). Required if main.runtime.enabled: true . Three files: the browser attempt key, the PAT signing key and the Form users JSON. Required if using Form or mixed authentication. The auth document is elitea.auth.form.v2 : it has no redis block, because the Form sign in state is in PostgreSQL, and the attempt key is credentials.attempt key file . The Form users JSON is a sign in path only when main.env.ELITEA FORM LOGIN ENABLED is "true" ; Form sign in is off by default. Required on both main and gateway; must be identical. HMAC key for signing/verifying identity headers. Two settings with no chart default The chart refuses to render while either of these is empty — there is no safe guess for either, and a guessed value would look armed while guarding nothing: | Setting | What it is | | | | | llmGateway.env.GATEWAY SELF LLM ORIGINS | Every origin that reaches this deployment's /llm surface, public and in cluster, comma separated — e.g. https://elitea.example.com/llm/v1,http://elitea main:8080/llm/v1 . | | llmGateway.egressPosture | "allowlist" (only hosts in GATEWAY EGRESS ALLOWLIST / governance rows) or "public unrestricted" (any public host, until the first governance row narrows it). Private network reachability follows only from an entry that explicitly names a private address or block — never from the posture alone. | Also required: platform.aiProjectId , the id of the platform's public/shared project — it must name a project schema ( p ) that already exists. It fills main.env.ELITEA AI PROJECT ID , llmGateway.env.ELITEA AI PROJECT ID and web.env.VITE PUBLIC PROJECT ID at once; helm template refuses a values file where the three copies disagree. Choose a values file The chart's own defaults. The runtime plane, the worker, elitea vector with the bundled Qdrant, DeepWiki and Inventory are on , one switch each ( main.runtime.enabled , worker.enabled , vector.enabled with qdrant.enabled , deepwiki.enabled , inventory.enabled ); set one to false explicitly to leave it out. The base file alone does not render: the values only you know (the authentication document and its public origin , the public project, DEPLOYMENT URL , the worker's identity, the git allowlists, the network policy peers, the gateway's self origins and egress posture) are listed together in one refusal, so a first helm template is the checklist. Qdrant needs a PersistentVolumeClaim ( qdrant.persistence , 50Gi on the default StorageClass). The full capability set, matching docker compose.standalone full.yml — every capability flag on, the runtime plane on (agent execution, index ingest), sized for postgresql.maxConnections: 200 across up to main.autoscaling.maxReplicas: 4 . Needs both the runtime material Secret and the auth material Secret. This is the reference production shape. The cheapest install that can seed an AI provider credential through the product's own API instead of hand written SQL: production (Form) authentication plus ELITEA CONFIGURATIONS ENABLED , no runtime plane — no agent execution, no chat. Needs the auth material Secret, but no Redis, no runtime material Secret and no worker: the Form sign in state is in PostgreSQL. Google Kubernetes Engine with no static cloud credential: Cloud SQL with sslmode=require and a hand prepared database, keyless GCS through Workload Identity, the GKE Ingress with its BackendConfig and FrontendConfig, Google's load balancer ranges in the NetworkPolicy, and every Secret from Secret Manager through externalSecrets . Sized for about 4 vCPU and 9 GiB of requests in steady state, with every default on. See Deploy on GKE with Argo CD. A minimal single replica shape (image tag shadow v0.1 , DATABASE URL inlined for a throwaway environment, autoscaling and the pod disruption budget both off). Use it for a disposable smoke/shadow environment, not as a production starting point. Install: one chart, one namespace One release installs everything, in one namespace. NATS requires TLS and a client certificate from every client (mTLS, no anonymous or password access), and those certificates come from the chart's own NATS CA, a namespaced cert manager Issuer , so NATS, its bootstrap and the platform share the release's namespace by construction. cert manager must be installed first. From a clone, build the chart's dependencies first. The upstream NATS chart and the sandbox runtime installer are pinned in the committed Chart.lock , and charts/ is never committed: The published chart is the recommended source: oci://ghcr.io/elitea ng/charts/elitea version in place of the path. Its package carries the same values files ( helm pull untar to read them) and both dependencies, so it needs no helm dependency build . In an air gapped network, mirror that OCI chart; do not build from a clone. The chart issues each NATS client (elitea main, the LLM gateway, the scheduler, the worker) its own certificate and renders tls://elitea nats.elitea.svc.cluster.local:4222 for it — no NATS credential goes in any value. The stream and KV bootstrap is a post install,post upgrade hook Job; until it has run, the workloads restart, then settle. helm install wait waits for workloads that wait for the streams the bootstrap hook creates, and that hook runs only after the wait. Leave wait off the first install; later upgrades may use it. For three NATS nodes, add f values nats ha.yaml (it raises the bootstrap's replica count too). To use a NATS you run yourself, set nats.enabled=false and point natsClient. at it. Under ArgoCD the same chart orders itself with sync waves — see GitOps with ArgoCD. helm template catches missing prerequisites before any kubectl apply: The migration job and DB bootstrap elitea migrate runs as a pre install hook; the database may start empty. The dbInit Job (hook weight 20) handles CREATE DATABASE for the agent state database before migrations run. It creates no extension. First admin bootstrap A fresh database seeds exactly one administrator, dev@elitea.ai , with no password on a single sign on deployment — name your own account instead through identity.initial global admins (a YAML list, wins when the authentication document has one) or main.env.ELITEA INITIAL GLOBAL ADMINS (comma separated, the usual path for a single sign on only install with no document). With Form sign in off (the default), the first OIDC or SAML sign in that matches an entry — oidc: , saml: , or email: for an OIDC login with a verified address — is your first administrator. Write Form logins there only if you enable Form sign in. An entry is oidc: , saml: , or email: (matches only when the id token asserts email verified: true ). The grant is one shot: an account that already holds any administration role is left as is; one with none receives the grant on its next sign in. For OIDC with a verified e mail address, use email: . You know this value before the first sign in, so you can set it at install time. For other cases, sign in once and open Settings › Profile . Each Sign in reference row shows one exact value that the list accepts, for example oidc: or saml: . Click a row to copy it. Add the value to the list, upgrade the release, and sign in again. You do not need to query the database. See Install Elitea for the browser side walkthrough of this same step. Capability flags this install serves cmd/elitea main gates whole route groups on these variables. values.yaml sets every one; values standalone.yaml is the reference production set. ELITEA CONFIGURATIONS ENABLED ships empty in the base chart — helpers.tpl derives "true" automatically once any authentication is configured and ELITEA AI PROJECT ID is set; a stated value always overrides the derivation. | Flag | Default install | values standalone.yaml | Needs | | | | | | | ELITEA ARTIFACTS ENABLED | on | on | object storage configured | | ELITEA CONFIGURATIONS ENABLED | derived | on | any authentication and ELITEA AI PROJECT ID | | ELITEA PROJECT INFO ENABLED | off | on | production authentication | | ELITEA CONFIGURATIONS MUTATION ENABLED | off | off | ELITEA CONFIGURATIONS ENABLED and runtime.enabled | | ELITEA INDEX TYPES ENABLED | off | on | production authentication | | ELITEA APPLICATION SKILLS ENABLED | off | on | production authentication | | ELITEA RUNTIME ENABLED ( main.runtime.enabled ) | on | on | production authentication and runtime material | ELITEA CONFIGURATIONS MUTATION ENABLED stays off in every shipped values file. It composes a second, asynchronous write route that would win the path from the compatibility route every install currently serves — and the compatibility route already writes status ok inline from the same admission decision, which is what makes a saved credential usable. Turning it on is a separate cutover with its own client side work, not a fix for an invisible credential. Post install checks /readyz and /startupz are deliberately not routed by the edge: their bodies name each dependency's state. The chart's probes reach them on the pod directly. /admin/app — sign in as the account you named above. /docs/ (this site) and /api/docs (the OpenAPI UI) should both resolve once main.ingress (or a route of your own to elitea main) publishes the platform: elitea main relays /app and /docs to elitea web itself. See Troubleshooting for what each endpoint answers and the application level Health tab it complements. What a Kubernetes install does NOT give you The chart provisions no database. The migration hook fails against a cluster where PostgreSQL does not already exist or where the Secret/host settings have not been pointed at it. NATS, by contrast, is part of the release: elitea main's live updates — the project SSE stream and canvas presence — need it with JetStream ( ELITEA EVENTS NATS URL , derived from the natsClient block), and so does the runtime plane: its command bus is JetStream in the RUNTIME account ( ELITEA RUNTIME NATS URL , as the elitea main runtime identity), consumed by the workers from their own WORKER account. The chart refuses main.runtime.enabled with no NATS to publish to. No Ingress or HTTPRoute renders until main.ingress.enabled: true . Then it is one / rule to elitea main, which is the whole edge: elitea main redirects / to /app/ , relays /app and /docs to elitea web, and serves its MCP endpoint under /app itself. On GKE, main.ingress.gke adds the BackendConfig and FrontendConfig the Google load balancer needs. The bundled server lives in the release's namespace, signed by the chart's namespaced elitea nats ca Issuer. To use a NATS you run elsewhere, set nats.enabled: false , back a cert manager ClusterIssuer with a CA used for NATS only, and point natsClient.service , natsClient.namespace and natsClient.tls.issuerRef at it; the bootstrap's identities follow natsClient ( natsBootstrap.tls.certificate.issuerRef ). The bootstrap Job still runs against your server unless natsBootstrap.enabled: false . Your server must run JetStream and map the same client identities, or elitea main refuses to start. deploy/helm/elitea/NATS.md has the contract. Anyone who may create a cert manager Certificate in the NATS namespace, or read its Secrets (the CA key is one), can obtain any NATS client identity. Restrict both with RBAC; the optional approver policy ( nats.security.approverPolicy ) limits what the NATS issuers sign. See deploy/helm/elitea/NATS.md . Every sensitive value is a Kubernetes Secret — see "Secrets to create beforehand" above. In production, turn on externalSecrets and the chart renders an ExternalSecret for each one from your secret manager's store; Deploy on GKE with Argo CD shows it with Google Secret Manager. Continue to GitOps with ArgoCD to run this same install declaratively, or Configuration for the operator facing settings after the pods are Ready. To run desktop threads sent to the cloud, add Cloud executor on Kubernetes. {/ source: deploy/README.md:232 341 (values table, first admin), deploy/README.md:389 431 (distribution), deploy/README.md:433 605 (capability flags), deploy/README.md:607 730 (runtime + auth material), deploy/README.md:859 918 (what K8s does not give you); deploy/helm/elitea/values standalone.yaml:1 30, 105 260; deploy/helm/elitea/values auth minimal.yaml:1 70; deploy/helm/elitea/values staging.yaml:1 25; deploy/helm/elitea/values.yaml:344 360, 2306 2358 (secrets); deploy/argocd/applications/elitea.yaml (hook and wave ordering); docs/UPGRADING.md ("One chart: NATS bundled", "One edge route", "Helm 4"); deploy/helm/elitea/NATS.md; deploy/helm/elitea/templates/main/migrate job.yaml, templates/worker/runtime session job.yaml, templates/dbInit/job.yaml (hook weights) /}

title: Day-2 operations
text: Running the platform after install: upgrading it safely, changing its master key, scaling its four independently scaled components, and where to look when something breaks. Upgrades Point your ArgoCD Application (or helm upgrade ) at the new published chart version — see GitOps with ArgoCD. The published chart's image.tag already tracks that version. elitea migrate is a pre install,pre upgrade Helm hook. Helm applies and awaits every such hook — including the migration Job — before it touches any of the release's other resources, so new pods never roll against an un migrated schema. A failed migration aborts the release , and the previously running pods keep serving; nothing is torn down until the new version proves it can start. Or, under ArgoCD, let selfHeal: true reconcile the bumped targetRevision /parameter automatically. helm rollback elitea (or the ArgoCD equivalent, argocd app rollback elitea ) returns to the previous release's values and image tags. The migration hook runs again on the way there — a rollback that also needs a schema rollback is a database operation this mechanism does not perform for you. Changing SECRETS MASTER KEY The key has three states, and moving between them is not symmetric: | State | Effect | | | | | Set, valid | Every project's vault key is wrapped with it; rows are Fernet tokens. | | Not set | The service still starts, with a log warning — every project key is stored in the clear . Anyone who can read the database can open every project secret. | | Set, malformed | The service refuses to start , naming the variable. | Rows written under one key (or under no key) do not become readable when the key changes — there is no in place re encryption. To rotate the key: run scripts/rewrap centry vault.py against a copy of the database first. It rewraps the project key and never rewrites the secret values themselves, so a rotation that fails partway leaves the plaintext secrets untouched. Both elitea main and elitea llm gateway read the same centry.secrets key table. Give the same value to every service that reads it — two services with two answers would put two row formats in one table, and neither could read what the other wrote. Scaling Three components carry a native HorizontalPodAutoscaler ; the fourth uses a different mechanism on purpose: CPU/memory HPA, minReplicas: 2 / maxReplicas: 10 by default. Scaling this past what postgresql.maxConnections was sized for is refused at render time — see Production deployment overview. CPU/memory HPA. Stateless; a rollout is safe at any time. Scales on concurrent /llm streams ( gateway llm sse active connections ) through KEDA's Prometheus trigger or a custom metrics adapter, and falls back to CPU when neither is there. Off by default ( llmGateway.autoscaling.enabled ). The chart picks the source it can see and refuses one you name that is missing; see Scaling. No native HPA. An agent execution spends most of its life waiting on a model, so CPU/memory never reflects backlog. Queue depth autoscaling through KEDA is available ( worker.autoscaling , off by default) — it scales on the worker durable's waiting plus held commands on the NATS command bus ( num pending + num ack pending , read from the NATS monitoring port). The chart refuses to install a KEDA ScaledObject unless KEDA is actually present, rather than creating an object nothing reads. KEDA's scaler reads /jsz on the bundled NATS's headless service, port 8222 (plain HTTP, no credential); the NATS NetworkPolicy admits the KEDA operator there ( nats.networkPolicy.monitoringFrom ). A scaler that cannot connect reports no lag, which scales the fleet down while the backlog grows; the chart cannot detect this for you. The agent worker's own replica count stays correct at 1 — the database enforces one active claim per execution regardless ( execution claims active idx is unique on (execution id, generation) while a claim is live) — but scaling out is not free capacity by default. Measure the command bus durable's delivery rate before raising it or turning KEDA on; a long cooldownSeconds (300s default) is deliberate, because an in flight agent execution can run for minutes and a short cooldown turns every quiet moment into a round of terminations. Backups Not provisioned or backed up by any chart here — bring your own PostgreSQL operator/managed service and its backup mechanism. The connection budget reserves headroom ( reservedConnections: 25 ) explicitly for backup tooling and interactive psql alongside the application's own pools, so a backup job does not compete with the application for its last connection slot. Also brought by you — the chart only creates the bucket (optionally, via objectInit ) and sets its retention lifecycle. Use your object store's own versioning/replication for backup. NATS runs inside the elitea release (the bundled upstream NATS chart, its JetStream volume elitea nats js elitea nats 0 ), but its state is rebuildable; back up the JetStream KV buckets and stream through NATS's own tooling if their loss matters to you. Losing the JetStream store resets budget enforcement counters to zero, but does not lose spend history: the Usage page's accumulators are written independently by elitea scheduler's write back consumer from the gateway's billing deltas, not read out of the counter itself. runtime session init (or the Helm workload session Job) is what authorizes the agent worker's certificate identity in elitea runtime.workload sessions ; a database restored from a backup that predates it has no such row. Re run standalone stack.sh seed runtime (compose) or re trigger the workload session hook Job (Helm) to recover, rather than assuming a restore alone brings chat back. CI/CD: what publishes, and how it's checked .github/workflows/publish.yml never runs on a merge. It has three channels: | Channel | Started by | Version | Moves latest | | | | | | | release | dispatch from main | semantic release from the conventional commits since the last stable tag | yes, and . | | nightly | the 02:07 UTC schedule on main , skipped when nothing landed since the last one | nightly. . (a GitHub pre release) | no | | dev | dispatch from any branch | dev. (a GitHub pre release) | no | is the version a release would cut from that ref now, so a pre release sorts before the release it previews; the newest 14 pre releases of each channel are kept, with their images and charts, and older ones are deleted. Cut a release with gh workflow run publish.yml ref main f channel=release . A stable release also deploys the docs site. Every channel also attaches the signed and notarised macOS desktop app (Apple silicon, Elitea aarch64.dmg ) to its GitHub release. For every channel, every first party image is built, scanned twice (once against the artefact this release actually pushes, in addition to a same day CI scan of a rebuild), and cosign signed keylessly before the charts ( elitea , which carries NATS and the sandbox runtime installer, and elitea sandbox runtime , still published on its own) are packaged, stamped with that version, pushed to oci://ghcr.io/elitea ng/charts/ , and signed the same way. The chart job runs strictly after the images it references are pushed, so a chart never reaches the registry pointing at a tag that does not exist yet. If any stage fails, a rollback job deletes everything that stage's run had already pushed — charts and images alike. Separately, .github/workflows/helm install smoke.yml installs the chart into a real kind cluster (not just helm template ) on every PR touching deploy/helm/ , and asserts every pod reaches Ready, the DeepWiki/Inventory provider pod's two containers run the runners the chart set, the facade's provider registration is healthy over its mTLS hop, and a fixture generation completes end to end — it installs the chart's shipped defaults (the runtime plane, the bundled Qdrant and elitea vector , DeepWiki and Inventory), with the worker, the LLM gateway, the web UI and the scheduler off for weight, so it proves the chart installs cleanly, not the full product. Security posture Every published image is scanned by Trivy against the exact digest this release pushes (not a same day rebuild), gated by scripts/ci/image scan gate.sh ; an exempted finding must be recorded in .github/image scan exempt.txt rather than silently passing. The agent execution plane's three listeners (control, output, content) all require and verify a client certificate; there is no cleartext mode. The runtime and auth material both arrive as Kubernetes Secrets, copied by an init container into an owner only emptyDir because a plain Secret volume cannot satisfy the permission profile the code enforces. elitea main deletes caller supplied X Auth and X Elitea identity headers itself, before any route runs, and reads no X Auth header as an identity, so a plain Ingress that forwards them is safe. The chart's HTTPRoute removes the same names again ( main.ingress.stripIdentityHeaders ) as defence in depth. Required, not optional, on both elitea main and the gateway, and the two must agree — see Install with Helm. Troubleshooting Operator facing infrastructure checks ( /healthz , /readyz , the application level Health tab, common agent/pipeline/toolkit errors) live on one page: see Troubleshooting. This page covers the deployment mechanics around those checks; that one covers what each check actually reports. {/ source: deploy/README.md:920 976 (SECRETS MASTER KEY three states, rewrap script), deploy/README.md:163 231 (hook ordering, migration abort behaviour); deploy/helm/elitea/values.yaml:80 136 (connection budget/reservedConnections), 1567 1573, 1702 1712, 2452 2532 (main/web/gateway HPAs), 2896 3070 (worker.implementation, KEDA autoscaling); .github/workflows/publish.yml:1 20, 155 177, 361 431, 718 934 (release pipeline, scan then sign, chart packaging); .github/workflows/helm install smoke.yml:1 70 (what the smoke job proves); deploy/README.md:632 679 (runtime material init container), deploy/README.md:106 111 (runtime session init recovery) /}

title: Production deployment overview
text: Elitea's Kubernetes path is one Helm chart, elitea , for everything: the platform, NATS JetStream with its stream bootstrap, the vector store and, where a cluster needs it, the sandbox runtime installer. ArgoCD syncs it as one Application through an app of apps root. This page is the map; Deploy from scratch walks a complete first install, Install with Helm is the shorter reference, and Deploy on GKE with Argo CD is the GitOps install on Google Cloud. A one host Compose stack ( docker compose.standalone full.yml ) runs the same topology for evaluation and small teams — see Install Elitea. This section covers the Kubernetes path only. Target topology Every arrow into the worker and the NATS command bus is mutually authenticated (mTLS; the command bus is NATS JetStream, elitea main publishing as its own identity and the workers pulling from their own account) — that plane's material is described in Install with Helm and deploy/runtime/README.md . DeepWiki and Inventory are two instances of the same subapp host pattern: a Go host process reaching a Rust engine sidecar over a Unix socket inside one pod. What the chart creates, and what you bring The chart is one release — elitea main and its migration Job, elitea web, the scheduler, the LLM gateway, the agent worker, the OTel collector, the database preparation Job, the DeepWiki and Inventory provider services with their own migration Jobs, and the vector store: elitea vector ( vector.enabled ) with Qdrant ( qdrant.enabled , the upstream qdrant chart bundled like NATS), which indexing and the native DeepWiki and Inventory engines need. The runtime plane, the worker, the vector store, DeepWiki and Inventory are all on by default, one switch each ( .enabled: false leaves one out). NATS JetStream and its bootstrap Job are in the same release ( nats.enabled , on by default), ordered ahead of the workloads; the sandbox runtime installer ( sandboxRuntime.enabled ) is off unless a k3s or EKS cluster needs gVisor on its nodes. No chart provisions it. Point postgresql.existingSecret at a Secret holding the DSN; the database may start empty (the migration Job bootstraps the schema itself), but an administrator DSN is still needed for CREATE DATABASE . Plain PostgreSQL is enough: no extension, because every vector is in Qdrant. cert manager must be installed: the bundled NATS CA, every NATS identity and the in cluster mTLS hops are its Certificate s. Secrets come from you, or from your secret manager through the chart's externalSecrets block (External Secrets Operator). An S3 compatible endpoint for artifacts and DeepWiki/Inventory output. The bucket must exist before the first sync (or set objectInit.enabled: true for a self hosted S3 compatible store you administer directly); a missing bucket lets the deployment look green and then crash loop on the next boot step. No Ingress or HTTPRoute renders until main.ingress.enabled is on. Then it is one / rule with elitea main as the sole backend, and that is the whole edge: elitea main relays /app and /docs to elitea web. Your ingress controller or Gateway, DNS and public certificate are yours; on GKE, main.ingress.gke adds what the Google load balancer needs. The chart consumes an authentication configuration document or OIDC ISSUER URL ; it issues no certificates of its own beyond the in cluster mTLS hops (cert manager issuers, brought by you). Sizing: the PostgreSQL connection budget The runtime plane (agent execution) opens six isolated connection pools per elitea main replica — 36 connections beyond the primary pool — and they may not share capacity. values standalone.yaml sizes for this explicitly: at postgresql.maxConnections: 200 and main.autoscaling.maxReplicas: 4 , four replicas cost roughly 4 × 42 = 168 connections, inside the 175 left after reservedConnections: 25 (interactive psql , backup tooling, the migration and dbInit Jobs). The chart's own guard ( elitea main.validateConnectionBudget ) refuses to render a topology that would exceed the stated ceiling, rather than letting it surface later as FATAL: sorry, too many clients already on whichever component connects next. When the server cannot hold the replicas you need, turn on the chart's transaction mode PgBouncer ( pgbouncer.enabled ) and point the elitea main db DSN at its Service. Every elitea main replica then shares one server side pool. The migration Jobs, the gateway and the worker keep their direct connections, which reservedConnections covers. Published artefacts Every chart ( elitea , and the standalone elitea sandbox runtime ) and every first party image is built, cosign signed (keyless) and pushed to ghcr.io/elitea ng by the release job in .github/workflows/publish.yml , after the images they reference are already pushed and signed. An OCI chart reference resolves by SemVer, so version is required in practice — there is no floating tag to fall back on. The in repo chart defaults to "latest" ; the published chart's image.tag is rewritten to the release version so it never installs a stale cached layer. Image manifests verify the same way, against ghcr.io/elitea ng/ : . If any part of a release fails, the rollback job deletes the pushed charts along with the images — a chart never stays published pointing at an image that got rolled back. Continue to Install with Helm for the step by step install, or GitOps with ArgoCD if you are deploying through the app of apps. {/ source: deploy/README.md:163 431 (chart table, composition decision, distribution); deploy/helm/elitea/values standalone.yaml:1 20 (connection budget); deploy/helm/elitea/values.yaml:80 136 (postgresql.maxConnections, reservedConnections); deploy/helm/elitea/Chart.yaml (chart description, dependencies); .github/workflows/publish.yml (chart matrix); docs/UPGRADING.md (one chart, one edge route) /}

title: Scaling
text: Every Elitea workload either has an autoscaler or is a singleton for a stated reason. All the autoscalers are on by default . The rule behind them: an autoscaler scales on its best signal when that signal's controller and source are present, and on CPU when they are not . An autoscaler that reads a metric nothing publishes holds the fleet at its floor while the load grows, and reports nothing. So each source below is detected from the cluster, installed by the release, or stated by you. A source you name but do not have is refused at render time, with the reason. What scales on what | Component | Autoscaler | Scales on | Needs | Default range | | | | | | | | elitea main | HPA | CPU (70 %) and memory (80 %) | metrics server | 2 to 8 | | elitea web | HPA | CPU (70 %) | metrics server | 2 to 6 | | elitea vector | HPA | CPU (70 %) | metrics server | 2 to 6 | | LLM gateway | KEDA prometheus + CPU | sum(gateway llm sse active connections) in the namespace, 40 streams per replica | KEDA, Prometheus scraping :8083/metrics | 2 to 4; the ceiling divides the degraded mode budget cap (see The gateway's expected replicas) | | | HPA, Pods metric | gateway llm sse active connections per pod, through custom.metrics.k8s.io | a custom metrics adapter | | | | HPA | CPU (70 %) | metrics server | | | Agent worker | KEDA nats jetstream + CPU | consumer lag on the agent command stream; one replica per delivery max concurrency (32) commands | KEDA | 1 to 10 | | | HPA | CPU (70 %) | metrics server | | | DeepWiki | KEDA prometheus + CPU | running invocations plus the generations refused fleet full in the last 5 minutes, one replica per ELITEA DEEPWIKI MAX PARALLEL WORKERS | KEDA, Prometheus scraping the host's admin port | 1 to 3 | | | KEDA postgresql + CPU | the same, counted in the invocations table | KEDA, the host's database | | | | HPA | CPU (70 %) | metrics server | | | Inventory | as DeepWiki | running ingestions, counted in inventory graph.invocations | as DeepWiki; the host's database is required for more than one replica | 1 to 3 | | OTel collector | HPA | CPU (70 %) | metrics server | 1 to 3 | | Egress proxy (off by default) | HPA | CPU (70 %) | metrics server | 2 to 6 | | Scheduler | none: an active/active pair | scheduler.replicaCount 1 or 2 | | 2 | | NATS, Qdrant | none: stateful | fixed size; see High availability | | 1 | | PgBouncer (off by default) | none: a singleton | | | 1 | | Sandbox supervisor (off by default) | none: a singleton | | | 1 | source: auto (the default for the gateway, the worker, DeepWiki and Inventory) picks the first source that is available, in the order of the table. Name a source in .autoscaling.source to require it: a named source that is not available is refused, with the reason. Every KEDA ScaledObject also has a CPU trigger ( targetCPUUtilizationPercentage , 70 % by default). The HPA that KEDA makes takes the larger of the two, so the component still scales when Prometheus or the database cannot be read. A CPU HPA without metrics server reports FailedGetResourceMetric and holds the Deployment at minReplicas . That is the old fixed count, not an outage. Turn an autoscaler off with .autoscaling.enabled: false ; the Deployment then runs replicaCount . While an autoscaler owns a Deployment, the chart renders no replicas: field on it. A value there would be written back by every helm upgrade and every Argo CD sync, snap the fleet to replicaCount , and leave the autoscaler to scale it out again. DeepWiki and Inventory An invocation runs on the replica that accepted it, from start to end. Its row is in a shared invocation store in the engine's database (DeepWiki: invocations ; Inventory: inventory graph.invocations ), so any replica answers a poll, a cancel or a deletion: A cancel goes to the owner replica over NATS. The owner also reads the stop requests on its own rows at each claim check (10 s), so a cancel arrives without NATS too. A deletion stops the matching runs on every replica, and waits until they end. While it runs, a stop fence ( host stop fences ) refuses a new run that matches it on every replica, so a generation that starts during the deletion cannot publish the index again. When a replica stops, another replica marks the runs it left behind as terminal. Generation slots are fleet wide . A replica writes its slot count ( ELITEA DEEPWIKI MAX PARALLEL WORKERS ) in host replicas , and a heartbeat apart from the claim check keeps the row live. A generation is admitted while the running generations are fewer than the slots of all live replicas that admit work. A replica whose own slots are full still admits while the fleet has a free slot (it runs above its own count; the fleet total is the bound), so a call that round robin sends to a busy replica is not refused while a sibling is idle. A replica that drains, or that is not live, leaves the count with its slots and its running generations together. A call is never queued: when no slot is free, the call is accepted and ends at once with service busy ("All N generation slots are busy"), and the UI shows that message. The slots page reports the same fleet numbers. The setting is per replica , so the fleet's capacity grows with the fleet: fleet slots = ELITEA DEEPWIKI MAX PARALLEL WORKERS × live replicas that admit work. The default is 1 slot per replica and 1 to 3 replicas, so 1 to 3 generations at once. One slot per replica is deliberate: a generation holds a whole engine (memory, CPU and 4 database connections), and a second generation on the same pod slows both. To run more generations at once, raise deepwiki.autoscaling.maxReplicas (capacity added on demand), raise minReplicas (capacity always there), or raise the slots per replica together with the engine's memory and the connection budget. With source: cpu (no KEDA), a refused generation does not make the fleet grow: only CPU does. If your users start generations at the same time, set minReplicas to the number of generations you expect at once, or install KEDA so the refused demand counts. The generations refused because the whole fleet was full are part of the scaling signal: elitea subapp slot refusals total{reason="fleet full"} on the admin port, or the rows whose result has busy reason fleet full . Without them the running count could never be above the slots, and the fleet could not grow. The other reasons ( draining , and local full on a one replica install without a database) are not demand and are not counted. More than one replica needs the host's database ( postgresql.existingSecret , or deepwiki.secrets.ELITEA DEEPWIKI DATABASE URL and inventory.secrets.ELITEA INVENTORY DATABASE URL ). For Inventory, the host also needs the migrate Job that creates its tables (the host runner sidecar and inventory.migrate.enabled: true ); without the Job the host gets no database URL. Without a store, the chart refuses maxReplicas above 1: each replica would keep its invocations in memory. With a fixture runner and no database, set deepwiki.autoscaling.enabled: false or inventory.autoscaling.enabled: false . Singletons and their high availability story | Workload | Why one | Availability | | | | | | Scheduler | Not CPU bound. Every job is safe on two replicas: singleton work takes an advisory lock, the retention sweep uses SKIP LOCKED , the write back consumer deduplicates. A third replica adds only connections, so the chart refuses more than 2. | Two replicas by default, a PDB and spread: one keeps working while the other moves. | | NATS | Stateful (JetStream). | values nats ha.yaml : three nodes, streams replicated three times. | | Qdrant | Stateful (the vectors). | values qdrant ha.yaml : a three node cluster. | | PgBouncer | Its pool is counted once in the connection budget; a second replica would double it. | A restart takes seconds; elitea main retries its connections. | | Sandbox supervisor | It writes a fixed owner identity in the sandbox ledger and keeps its live runs in memory. Two would fight over the same runs. Recreate strategy. | A restart reconciles the ledger; runs in flight end as failed and are started again. | | Sandbox image warmup | A DaemonSet: one pod per node by design. | | How gRPC load spreads A gRPC client keeps one HTTP/2 connection and sends every call on it. Behind a ClusterIP Service that is one replica for the life of the connection, whatever the autoscaler adds. So the hops that carry the load use client side round robin over a headless Service (one connection to each replica), and each server closes connections after a maximum age , so the clients reconnect and see new replicas: | Hop | Service | Server connection age | | | | | | elitea main → LLM gateway | headless elitea llm gateway grpc , round robin | 5 min | | elitea main → DeepWiki | headless elitea deepwiki grpc , round robin | 1 min | | elitea main → Inventory | headless elitea inventory grpc , round robin | 1 min | | elitea main → elitea vector | headless elitea vector grpc , round robin | ELITEA VECTOR MAX CONNECTION AGE SECONDS , 300 s | | the worker, the engines → elitea vector | ClusterIP elitea vector | ELITEA VECTOR MAX CONNECTION AGE SECONDS , 300 s | At its maximum age a connection closes gracefully: the calls on it finish, and the next call opens a new connection. The worker and the engines are Rust clients that dial the ClusterIP Service of elitea vector: each new connection goes to a replica that kube proxy selects, so their load spreads over the replicas within a few connection ages. The certificates do not change: elitea main still checks the ClusterIP Service name ( ELITEA DEEPWIKI SERVER NAME , ELITEA INVENTORY SERVER NAME , ELITEA VECTOR GRPC SERVER NAME ). Preconditions: KEDA and a custom metrics adapter KEDA and a custom metrics adapter are cluster wide : CRDs, plus an APIService each ( external.metrics.k8s.io for KEDA, custom.metrics.k8s.io for the adapter). A cluster runs one of each . Two of them fight over the same cluster scoped objects, and the scalers of whichever loses read nothing. | You have | Set | | | | | KEDA already in the cluster | nothing on helm install (the chart sees keda.sh/v1alpha1 ); scaling.keda.clusterInstalled: true for helm template and for Argo CD | | No KEDA, and you want the release to bring it | keda.enabled: true (the pinned kedacore chart, 2.21.0) | | A custom metrics adapter already | scaling.customMetrics.clusterInstalled: true where the chart cannot see it, and a rule for gateway llm sse active connections in that adapter | | No adapter, and the gateway should use one | prometheusAdapter.enabled: true and prometheusAdapter.prometheus.url (the pinned prometheus community chart, 5.3.0; its rules expose exactly the gateway metric and nothing else) | | Prometheus for the KEDA prometheus triggers | scaling.prometheus.serverAddress , plus a scrape: a PodMonitor (rendered by default wherever the Prometheus Operator's API is served), .metrics.scrapeAnnotations: true , or .metrics.scrapedExternally: true for a scrape config of your own | helm install and helm upgrade refuse keda.enabled or prometheusAdapter.enabled when they can see one that this release does not own. helm template and Argo CD cannot look into the cluster, so the install notes warn instead. Enable the bundled ones only on a cluster that has none. The Prometheus labels The generated prometheus queries select the release's namespace by a label.
