DeepWiki DeepWiki generates a searchable, AI authored wiki from a connected code repository — architecture summaries, source linked explanations, and a chat panel for asking questions about the codebase. Configuration: a code toolkit (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Azure DevOps Repos), an LLM model, a max token budget, and an embedding model. What you can do: Browse generated wiki pages and architecture diagrams. Ask questions in the wiki chat drawer as a continuable, multi turn session: it's saved server side, survives closing the drawer and reloading the page, and each new question carries earlier turns as context. List, resume, or delete this toolkit's past wiki chat sessions from the drawer's history control. Attach context to a question — specific wiki pages, small text files from your own machine (Markdown, plain text, CSV, source code; a few hundred KB and up to five files per question), or both together. Edit a generated page directly, or regenerate content for the connected repository. Inventory Inventory builds a knowledge graph of your codebase — components, dependencies, and ownership — so you can understand the code estate before planning a migration or refactor. Configuration: one or more repository toolkits (GitHub and Azure DevOps Repos by default) and the AI model settings used to build the graph. What you can do: Browse entities by name, type, layer, or source. Inspect a single component's properties and relationships. Ask questions about the ingested codebase in the Inventory chat panel. Review ingestion statistics for each connected source. Troubleshooting No toolkit of that type is configured yet in this project — configure one from Applications. Confirm the underlying repository toolkit's credentials are still valid, and check for a completion notification. Applications · Toolkits · Notifications

title: Help and support
text: Elitea offers two places to get help without leaving your work: the Help Center , a static hub of links your administrator configures, and the Support Assistant , a context aware AI chat widget. Help Center Select the ? button near the bottom of the sidebar to open the Help Center. In the desktop app, open the account menu at the foot of the sidebar and select Get help . The bug button beside the account button files a bug report on GitHub (Desktop account menu). Its default sections are Documentation , Release notes , Video library , Tutorials , and Interactive tours — each one links to whatever your administrator has configured under admin Configuration › Resources. Titles, descriptions, and links are fully customizable per deployment; a section with nothing configured shows "No links configured." When enabled, the header also shows the running platform version. If the Help Center looks empty, no links have been configured yet for this deployment — ask your administrator to add them. Support Assistant The Support Assistant is an optional, floating chat widget available from the sidebar when your administrator has turned it on. It tracks your current project, page, and any open entity (an agent, pipeline, toolkit, MCP, application, credential, or conversation), so its answers can be specific to what you're doing. What it can do: Answer questions in context, with full Markdown rendering — tables, code blocks, and Mermaid diagrams render as diagrams rather than raw text. Keep a history of your past conversations with it, reachable from the history icon in its header. Attach up to 10 files per message (images or documents, same limits as the main chat composer) by clicking the paperclip icon, dragging them onto the input, or pasting an image from the clipboard. Each attached file shows its own status chip — queued, uploading, or failed — and can be removed before you send. Expand to a fullscreen view, and follow your light/dark theme automatically. The Support Assistant authenticates using your personal access token. If your token is missing or expired, the widget fails to load or send messages — create or renew a token to fix it. Contact support Elitea does not ship a built in support ticket system. If something isn't covered by the Support Assistant or the documentation, reach out to your platform administrator directly, or use the Support Assistant itself for a first pass at a solution. Troubleshooting The feature is off for this deployment — ask your administrator to enable it in admin Features. Its backing agent may be misconfigured or missing valid credentials — this needs an administrator to check. Confirm the file is under the size limit and that you are attaching only one file per message. Settings › AI Providers · Personal tokens · Troubleshooting · FAQs

title: Internal tools
text: Internal tools are capabilities you turn on from Modules in chat or an agent's Tools section, without configuring an external toolkit. They come from a fixed platform catalogue ( features/agents/lib/internalTools.ts ) and are turned on per conversation or saved as an agent's default. Planner , Attachments , Data analysis and Smart tools selection run on the platform's agent worker. Image creation , Elitea MCP tools and Swarm mode are not run by the platform's worker: they show disabled with a "Not available on the Rust worker" note (agent Tools section) so you can see the gap before turning one on, and a run that still hits one gets a visible in conversation notice rather than the capability silently doing nothing (tracked in 866). Turn a module on Select + in the chat toolbar → Modules , then toggle the tool on. The setting lasts for the conversation. Open the agent, find Modules under Tools (select Show all if it is collapsed), toggle the tool, and Save . New conversations with that agent turn it on by default. Image creation Generates images from a text prompt and shows them inline, using an image generation model configured in AI Providers . Generated images are saved automatically to the project's attachments bucket, where you can also download or delete them later from Artifacts. This toggle is a chat conversation setting. To let an agent or pipeline generate or edit images as a step in its own logic — not just inline in chat — attach the ImageGen toolkit instead. Data analysis Runs pandas style analysis over a file you upload to the conversation — summaries, filtering, aggregation, and chart generation — driven entirely by natural language requests. Upload the file first, then ask for the analysis; generated charts and exported files are saved back to the conversation. For datasets larger than about 100 MB, or analysis needing custom code, use a Python based toolkit or a pipeline Code node instead. Attachments Lets the agent list, read and search the files attached to the conversation — including ones attached in earlier messages — with list attachments , read attachment and search attachment . A file small enough to fit is already shown to the model with your message; the tools reach the rest of a long document and the files from earlier turns. Each file is read from storage the first time the agent asks for it. Turn it on from the agent's Tools section (it is not in the chat toolbar). Planner Lets an agent write a plan for a multi step task and tick it off as it works: a title and numbered steps that move from pending to in progress to completed ( update plan , start step , complete step , get plan status , delete plan ). The plan belongs to the conversation: it is kept between messages and survives long conversations being summarised, and deleting the conversation removes it. The agent is also given short planning guidance in its instructions while the module is on. Swarm mode Turns a set of agents into peers that can hand off control to one another mid conversation, all sharing the same conversation history. The agent the user addresses is simply the default entry point; any peer can transfer to any other with a transfer to tool, and each hand off's task argument must be fully self contained — the receiving agent gets no other context. Swarm enabled agents cannot themselves be added as a child of another swarm agent. Smart tools selection Reduces token usage when an agent has many toolkits configured by binding only two meta tools ( get tool schema , invoke tool ) instead of every individual tool definition, loading real tool schemas on demand, and adding a compact index of the available toolkits and tools to the agent's instructions. Turn it on once a conversation or agent uses five or more toolkits — the more toolkits, the larger the savings. With fewer than 20 tools the module switches itself off for that message, since the meta tools would cost more than they save. A tool that needs your confirmation (a sensitive action) or a sign in to the service stays directly available to the agent instead of going through invoke tool , so approvals keep working exactly as without the module. The Planner, Attachments and this module apply to the agent you chat with; agents it calls as tools, and pipeline steps, do not get them. Troubleshooting Check the worker note under Internal tools: Image creation, Elitea MCP tools and Swarm mode are not run by the platform's worker — the conversation shows a visible notice rather than running them. No image generation model is configured for the project yet — add one in AI Providers. No module is available for the project at all — ask your administrator to configure at least one provider or toolkit. Chat: Modules · Agents: Modules · Elitea MCP tools · Attach files

title: Platform overview
text: Every menu in Elitea shares the same shell: a sidebar for navigation, a project selector, and a consistent set of list, search, and organization controls. This page covers what is common; each menu's own page covers what is specific to it. Sidebar The sidebar gives you access to every menu: Chat — conversations with models, agents, pipelines, toolkits, and MCP servers. Agents , Pipelines , Skills — the entities you build and manage. Toolkits — integrations with external services, plus MCP servers when your administrator has turned on MCP menu exposure. Apps — installed applications (DeepWiki, Inventory) and the catalog of applications you can request access to. Credentials , Artifacts — supporting resources: authentication and file storage. Catalog — the shared library of published agents and skills. Settings — project and personal configuration. At the bottom of the sidebar you'll also find a ? Help Center button, a notification bell, and your user profile. Project selector Use the project selector at the top of the sidebar to switch between your personal project — visible only to you — and any team projects you belong to, where entities are shared and collaboratively managed according to each member's role. Common list controls Most menus (Agents, Pipelines, Skills, Toolkits, Credentials) share the same dashboard pattern: Card view and table view , toggled from the top of the list. A search box scoped to the current menu — search does not span menus. Tag filters to narrow the list by category. Pinning — pin an item to keep it at the top of its list. Sorting (table view) by name, created date, type, or author. What's next Start with the menu you need: Conversations and participants. Build and run agents. Multi step workflows. Reusable instruction sets. External integrations and MCP servers. Deployable, focused solutions. Authentication for integrations. Shared file storage. Published agents and skills. For definitions of terms used across these menus, see the Glossary.

title: Pipelines
text: A pipeline is a visual, multi step workflow. Where an agent handles one task end to end, a pipeline breaks a process into nodes — agent calls, toolkit actions, decisions, and state updates — and connects them into a repeatable sequence. Create a pipeline Creation is two phases. First, fill in Name , Description , and optionally tags, a welcome message, conversation starters, and a step limit (default 25), then select Save — this creates the pipeline's base version. Saving unlocks the second phase: a three column editor with the configuration form on the left, the Flow/YAML editor in the center, and a live test chat on the right. Attach toolkits, agents, MCPs, and nested pipelines In Tools , use +Toolkit , +MCP , +Agent , and +Pipeline to attach existing resources for the workflow to call. This section only appears after the first save. State Every pipeline starts with two built in state variables: inputs (the triggering input) and messages (the conversation history). Add your own under State with a name and optional default value, then reference them in any node as {{state.variable name}} . State Modifier nodes read and write state during execution. Design the workflow Toggle between Flow and YAML at the top of the center panel. Add a node with + , choose its type, and connect nodes by dragging between their connection points. See Flow editor and the pipeline node reference for what each node type does and which ones the runtime actually executes. Edit the same workflow as YAML for advanced control, bulk changes, or replicating an existing pipeline. See YAML editor. File attachments Turn on Attachments in Modules to let users upload files in a pipeline conversation. Elitea adds an input attachments state variable automatically (and removes it if you turn attachments off) and injects a file storage toolkit at execution time — no manual toolkit setup needed. Test and execute The embedded chat panel lets you pick a model, adjust its settings, and run the pipeline interactively. Each execution is captured as a pipeline run with its inputs, outputs, and state changes; when context management is on, a Context Budget widget tracks token usage during the run. See Pipeline runs. Versions, publishing, export, and fork Pipelines version, publish, export/import, and fork the same way agents do — select Save As Version to branch, use the version dropdown to switch, and reach Export , Fork , and Publish from the toolbar's overflow menu. See Entity versioning, Import/export, and Forking. Troubleshooting Check that every node has its required tools and credentials configured, and that connections between nodes are complete. Verify credentials and network access for the external service that node calls. Confirm the receiving node's task field actually references the sending node's output variable — the input space listing organizes variables but does not pass them automatically. Pipeline overview · Pipeline structure · Credentials · Toolkits

title: AI Providers
text: AI Providers is where a project registers the models and storage it uses, and picks defaults for each category. Settings here apply at the project level for every member. Categories Language models, with Default, High tier, and Low tier selections. Used for indexing and semantic search. Powers the Image creation module in chat. Server side voice input. Server side spoken playback. Each category shows its configured models as cards with a provider icon, name, and a badge for Default, High tier, or Low tier. Select a card to edit it, if your role allows. Add a model or credential Choose a provider — OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Ollama, vLLM, or EPAM AI Dial — and provide its endpoint and key. One credential can back several models. Select + , choose the model category, and fill in a display name, the exact provider model identifier, and — for LLMs — context window, max output tokens, and whether it supports reasoning or vision. Use the category's dropdowns to make the new configuration the project default, or the high tier / low tier choice. The Name field must be the provider's own model identifier (or Azure deployment name) — not a display label. Refer to your provider's model list if a connection or generation fails. When an OpenAI or Anthropic model configuration uses AI Dial credentials, leave Supports Reasoning off — turning it on breaks connection validation for that combination. Speech recognition and text to speech fallbacks If no ASR model is configured, voice input falls back to the browser's Web Speech API; if no TTS model is configured, playback falls back to the browser's SpeechSynthesis API. Elitea determines ASR mode from the model name — whisper or transcribe selects batch transcription; anything else uses realtime streaming. Troubleshooting Confirm the model name matches the provider's identifier exactly and that your credential has access to it. Recheck the API key or token for typos or expiry, and confirm the endpoint URL is correct for your provider. Confirm a default ASR or TTS model is actually selected in this page, not just configured. Credentials · Project settings · Voice

title: Analytics and usage
text: Analytics and Usage give you two views of the same underlying activity: Analytics is about understanding how the project is used; Usage is about tracking spend against a budget. Analytics Settings › Analytics is available to any project member and requires the analytics enabled admin flag. Data is scoped to the currently selected project and refreshed from the API, cached for a few minutes. Choose a date range with the quick presets (Today/Last 7d/Last 30d/Last 90d) or custom From/To pickers, then switch between the tabs below. Each preset covers whole calendar days, from 00:00 on its first day to 23:59 today, and the To minute is included; for the last 24 hours or another exact window, set From and To by hand. From cannot be later than To. Daily charts group activity by UTC day, so outside UTC one local day can appear as two chart columns. The COST tile is billed spend per billing period (a calendar month), so it names the period it covers; under Today it is the month to date. Team size, AI adoption, LLM calls, tool runs, and the top adopters. Estimated LLM spend by day, by user, by model, by agent, and by tool. Input, output, and cache token usage by day, user, and model. Run counts, latency, and errors per agent or pipeline. Call counts, latency, and errors per tool. Per user activity, adoption, and the tools and agents they used. Request volume, error rates, and latency by event type. Select Export to Excel to download all tabs for the selected range as a single workbook. The LLM calls, tokens, active users and cost figures count completed model calls only. A model call is a request to a model route: chat, completions, embeddings, responses, messages, images, audio or realtime. A completed call is one the gateway answered with a status below 400. A budget refusal, a rate limit, a validation error or a provider failure is not counted, because the Usage tab does not bill it. The Agents & Pipelines tab counts every model call attempt, because it shows errors. The Health tab counts every request on every route, including model listings and requests to unknown paths, because it exists to show what failed. Analytics reads the gateway request log, which keeps 92 days of requests. The Costs tab's Cost by Agent and Cost by Tool tables answer which agent or tool a call is attributable to ( 875), the same estimate the by model and by user tables already give — derived from the request log and the price catalogue, not the figure the Usage tab's budget meter accounts. Cost by agent covers calls made from a runtime execution, which most direct /llm traffic is not; cost by tool attributes an execution's whole LLM spend to every tool that execution called, so a tool used inside a longer turn is not "what that one tool call cost" in isolation. Both tables are absent — not a zero row — for a deployment or a window that cannot correlate either dimension yet. Setting a spend LIMIT per agent or per tool is not available; see Budgets and LLM Governance. Usage Settings › Usage requires the cost budgets enabled admin flag and shows spend against the current monthly billing period for platform shared models only — models configured with your own provider credentials are billed by that provider and are not included. The page shows, for the current billing period: Spent this period , Limit (or Unlimited ) and Remaining . A usage meter with the percentage of the limit used. It changes colour past the project's warning threshold and again at the limit; a scope with no enforced limit says so instead of showing a meter. The billing period's start and end dates. A member who is not a project administrator sees the percentage and the period but not the amounts. When a request is refused because your own member budget is exhausted, the error links to this page scoped to you, showing your own spend against your own limit in this project. A warning banner appears as usage approaches its limit; once the limit is reached, requests to platform shared models are refused until the limit increases or the period resets. Select Refresh data (the circular arrow button in the header) to fetch the latest figures without reloading the page; if a refresh fails, the last loaded figures stay on screen with a note that they could not be updated. Troubleshooting The relevant admin flag ( analytics enabled or cost budgets enabled ) is off for this deployment — ask your administrator. API results are cached briefly; wait a moment, or select Refresh data on Settings › Usage. Your project or personal budget for shared models has been reached for the current period — wait for the reset or ask an administrator to raise the limit. Admin: Budgets and governance · Project settings

title: Desktop account menu
text: In the Elitea desktop app, the foot of the left sidebar shows who you are signed in as and which organization you are connected to: your picture, your name, and the deployment's name (for example Alex K · Acme Enterprise ). Select it to open the account menu. The bug button beside it files a bug report. What the menu holds | Item | What it does | | | | | Your email | The account you are signed in with. It is a label, not a link. | | Settings (⌘, / Ctrl+,) | Opens Settings in a window over the app. Close it with the × button, Escape or a click outside it to return to the page you were on. | | Usage | Opens Settings › Usage. It appears only when usage reporting is enabled for you. | | Credentials | Opens the Credentials page. It appears only if you can see credentials. | | Catalog | Opens the Elitea Catalog. | | Appearance | Choose System , Light or Dark . The choice is saved to your account, so the web app follows it too. | | Language | Choose the app's language (see Language). The window reloads in the new language: your session, folders and threads stay, but a message you have not sent yet is lost. | | Get help | Opens the Help Center (Help and support). | | What's new | Opens the release notes of the version you are running, on GitHub, in your browser. The version number is shown beside it. A nightly build opens the releases list at its entry. | | Troubleshoot | Opens Settings › Troubleshoot, where you can run the app's diagnostics. | | Sign out | Signs this computer out of the deployment and returns to the connect screen. | Appearance and Language open their choices beside the menu when you point at them, as menus in your operating system do; a click, or the right arrow key, opens them too. The left arrow key or Esc goes back. Every submenu in the app works this way, for example the agent's Version and the Step limit . Credentials, Catalog and the Help Center used to be rows in the sidebar. They moved to this menu so the list holds only the places you work in. The command palette (⌘K / Ctrl+K) still finds all of them. The sidebar and its project The top of the sidebar shows the project you are working in, under the search box. Everything below it belongs to that project. Select it to switch to another project: type part of a project's name to narrow the list, then use the arrow keys and Return, or click one. The list loads more projects as you scroll, so it stays quick when you belong to hundreds of projects. If a thread from a folder in the current project is open when you switch, the app closes it and shows the start screen of the new project. Local work lists the folders you opened in this project. Select the Local work heading to open the page with all your folders. A folder you open joins the selected project. A folder that has no project yet, for example one opened before projects were assigned, shows in every project marked No project until you give it one. To move a folder to another project, use its ⋯ menu ( Move to project ) or its right click menu ( Project ). The app asks you to confirm first. After the move, the folder shows under the other project, and its next threads use that project's models, credentials and budget. The files and past threads stay on your computer. Select the Chats heading to start a new chat, as + beside it does. Chats lists your chat folders and the date groups the app makes, such as Today and Previous 7 days . Each shows a folder icon that opens and closes. Archived opens your archived chats. Applications and Artifacts follow. Workshop groups Agents, Pipelines, Skills, Toolkits & Indexes and MCPs. Select it to open or close the group; the app remembers your choice. It is closed until you first open it, and it opens by itself when you go to one of its pages, for example from the command palette or a link. The message box Chats and Local work threads share one message box. Drag its top edge to make it taller or shorter (or focus the edge and use the arrow keys; double click resets it). What you type and do not send stays with that chat or thread until you come back. In a Local work thread the row under the text holds, from the left: + to attach images (you can also paste or drop them). The mode: Act (edits with approvals), Plan (plans, changes nothing) or Bypass (no approvals; the app warns you the first time). The agent and its version (point at Version to see the versions), and the model. ⋯ with Step limit : how many steps a turn may take. Point at it to pick the default, a preset, Unlimited or a number of your own. In a new thread of a git folder, Work in : This folder , or New worktree (see Work in a worktree). Send to cloud , or Take back for a thread running in the cloud (see Send a thread to the cloud), the language server status, the index icon, and a ring showing how much of the model's context the thread uses. Select the ring to open the Context tab. Send , which becomes Stop while a turn runs. The index icon shows the state of the folder's code index by its colour: grey when it is ready or off, the accent colour while it builds, orange when it is out of date and red after an error. Point at it to read the state, for example Index ready · 257.3K entities ; select it to open the Index tab on the right, where the index settings are. While a turn runs, in a chat or a thread, that round button is Stop until you type, then Send again: what you send waits in the Queued list at the top of the message box. Each queued message has Send now (stop the turn and send this message first), Edit (take it back into the message box) and Remove . Press Esc twice quickly to stop the turn from anywhere on the page; a single Esc still just closes a menu or dialog. Send a thread to the cloud A thread that may move to the cloud shows Send to cloud in the row under the text. Select it to review what is sent and send the thread. The small ⌄ beside it opens Handoff settings… , where you choose what stays on your computer. While the thread runs in the cloud, the same place shows Take back : select it to review the cloud's changes and apply them to your folder. Its ⌄ holds Erase cloud copy… , Open in chat and Handoff settings… . While the thread is on its way back it shows Returning and cannot be selected. When a thread cannot move (your deployment or project has the cloud executor off, or the thread has no messages yet), nothing is shown: the thread runs on your computer. The Changes tab The Changes tab on the right lists what each turn changed, newest first. Each turn is one line: the start of your message, the number of files and the lines added and removed. Select it to fold or unfold the turn; the newest turn starts unfolded. Point at a turn for Undo (or Restore folder after an undo). Each file is one row: its name, its folder in grey, the lines added and removed and a coloured letter, M modified, A added, D deleted or R renamed. Select a row to open its diff below it. Point at the row, or move to it with the keyboard, for Reveal in Finder , Open and Revert . The thread's title The thread's title at the top (folder › thread) opens a card with the folder's path, Reveal in Finder and Copy Path . To move the folder to another project, use the folder's menus in the sidebar. Language The desktop app is available in: | Language | | Language | | | | | | | | English | en | Русский | ru | | Deutsch | de | Українська | uk | | Español | es | 日本語 | ja | | Français | fr | 한국어 | ko | | Français (Canada) | fr CA | 简体中文 | zh CN | | Italiano | it | 繁體中文 | zh TW | | Nederlands | nl | العربية | ar | | Polski | pl | עברית | he | | Português (Brasil) | pt BR | فارسی | fa | | | | اردو | ur | Until you choose one, the app follows your operating system's preferred languages and picks the closest one it has. For example, Canadian French opens in Français (Canada), Belgian French in Français, and Hong Kong Chinese in 繁體中文. If none of your system's languages is available, the app opens in English. Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu are written right to left. In those languages the whole window is mirrored: the sidebar is on the right, and arrows and disclosure chevrons point the other way. File names, paths, code and product names keep their own direction. The app's menu bar (File, Edit, View…) and the menu bar icon's menu follow the same language. Your choice applies to this computer only. Signing out clears it, so the next person to sign in on a shared computer gets their system's language. Strings that have no translation yet are shown in English. Names of products and technical terms, such as MCP, DeepWiki or GitHub, are not translated. The translations are new, so if a label reads wrong, report it with the bug button. Work in a worktree A worktree is a separate copy of a git folder on its own branch. The agent works there while you keep using the folder, or while another thread works in it, so several tasks run side by side without touching each other's files. A new thread in a git folder starts with Work in set to New worktree . Write your message and send it: the app makes the worktree on a new elitea/… branch from the folder's current commit, opens the worktree's thread and sends the message there. To work in the folder itself, set Work in to This folder before you send. The app remembers your choice for each folder: after you pick This folder , the folder's next new thread starts on This folder too, until you pick New worktree again. New thread in a worktree in the folder's ⋯ or right click menu always starts on New worktree . A worktree shows under its folder in the sidebar, as one of the folder's threads with a branch icon, the thread's title, and how many commits it is ahead and how many files are not committed. Hover over the name to see the branch and where the worktree is. Hover actions: Diff shows what the task changed. Merge back previews the merge into the folder, then applies it as uncommitted changes. You can undo it. Remove deletes the worktree; the app asks first when it has uncommitted work. Its branch stays when it has commits. A worktree is never listed as a folder of its own, on the Local work page or in the command palette. Archive and delete threads Each thread under Local work has Archive and Delete… in its ⋯ menu (hover over the thread) and in its right click menu. They work the same for a thread that runs on this computer and one you sent to the cloud. Archive archives the thread's conversation, as archiving a chat does. The thread leaves Local work and shows under Archived in the Chats section. Unarchive it there and it shows under its folder again. Delete… asks first, then deletes the conversation and the thread's history on this computer. It can't be undone. When the thread works in a worktree, archiving or deleting it also removes the worktree. The app asks first, with Also remove its worktree checked; clear it to keep the worktree. The worktree's elitea/… branch stays when it has commits. When the worktree has changes that were never committed, the app asks again: Remove anyway deletes those changes, Keep the worktree leaves it in the sidebar. Unarchiving a thread whose worktree was removed restores its conversation, but the thread does not show under Local work again: its worktree is gone. If the thread you archive or delete is open, the app opens a new thread in its folder. When the app cannot reach your deployment At launch, or after your computer wakes, the network may not be up yet. The app keeps asking your deployment who you are, after 1, 2, 4 and 8 seconds and then every 15 seconds, and opens your work as soon as it answers. You don't need to restart it. If it stays on "Loading…", check your connection or VPN. Report a bug The bug button opens a new issue in the public elitea ng/elitea platform repository in your browser. The issue is prefilled with headings for what happened, what you expected and the steps to reproduce it, plus your app version, platform and language. Review it before you submit it. You need a GitHub account. The repository is public. The report never includes your deployment's address, your organization or your identity, and you should not add them, or any tokens or customer data. If logs would help, Settings › Troubleshoot shows them.

title: Memory
text: Settings › Memory has two, independent sections: Context management controls how much conversation history is kept as a single conversation grows, and Long term Memory is a persistent store of facts Elitea recalls in every later conversation in this project. Context management Turn context management on to have Elitea automatically manage history as it approaches a model's token limit. Max Context Tokens (default 64,000) — the ceiling for conversation history sent per request. Preserve Recent Messages (default 5) — the number of most recent messages always kept, regardless of the token ceiling. Context editing When context management is on, context editing clears older tool outputs from the sent history while keeping recent results, reducing token usage without losing recent detail. Automatic summarization With context management on, turn on summarization to have Elitea condense older messages into a summary once the conversation grows past a threshold, instead of dropping them outright. Summarization instructions — free text guiding style and focus of the generated summary. Target Summary Tokens (default 4,096) — the target length for each generated summary. Summarization only runs while context management is turned on — turning context management off disables summarization too, even if its own toggle is still on. Context management settings apply to every new conversation you start in Chat, Agents, and Pipelines in this project. Existing conversations, and conversations started by other users, keep their own settings. Long term Memory The Long term Memory section is a list of facts Elitea remembers about you — not tied to one conversation. A memory you save here is recalled by Elitea in every later conversation in this project , unlike context management above, which only manages history inside a single conversation. This is not the same feature as the Memory toolkit you can attach to an agent, pipeline, or conversation. The toolkit is a tool the model calls mid turn to read and write its own key/value store. Long term Memory here is never a tool call: your enabled memories are added to the assistant's context automatically, before a turn starts, whenever there is room and they are relevant to what you asked. Add a memory Select Add memory and describe a fact you want Elitea to know about you going forward — for example, "Prefers TypeScript over Python for new services." Optionally add comma separated tags to help you find it again later. New memories are enabled by default. Manage your memories Each row shows the memory's text and tags, with: An enabled switch — turn a memory off to stop it from being recalled without deleting it. Edit — change the text, tags, or enabled state. Delete — remove one memory permanently. Use the search box to filter the list by content or tag. Clear all deletes every memory in this project after a confirmation — this cannot be undone. Use my memories in chat is a master switch above the list. It is a shortcut, not a separate setting: turning it off disables every currently enabled memory in one action, and turning it on re enables every memory that was on before. There is nothing else it controls. Save a memory from a chat message You do not have to come back to Settings to save a memory. On any assistant answer in Chat, select the bookmark icon ( Remember this ) next to the message's other actions to save that answer's text as a new, enabled memory. A small confirmation icon shows it was saved. How recall works At the start of a chat turn, Elitea reads your enabled memories in this project and adds a bounded selection of them to the assistant's context, alongside the conversation's own history: Memories matching keywords in what you just typed are preferred, then the most recently saved ones fill any remaining room. Recall is bounded — only a limited number of memories, and a limited amount of text, are added to any one turn, so a large memory list never crowds out the rest of the conversation. A turn that used at least one memory shows a small "Using N memories" indicator next to its timestamp. Recall is best effort. If the memory store is briefly unavailable, the turn still runs — it simply proceeds without your recalled memories that one time. Troubleshooting Settings auto save on blur or on toggle — watch for a "Settings saved successfully" confirmation, and check numeric fields are within their valid range. Confirm context management is turned on — summarization is inactive whenever it is off. Confirm the memory's own enabled switch, and the "Use my memories in chat" master switch, are both on. Recall is also bounded — with many memories saved, an unrelated one may simply not have been selected for that particular turn. Long term Memory is scoped per project, the same as everything else in Settings. Switch projects to see that project's own memories. Context management · Chat · Memory toolkit

title: Notifications
text: Elitea delivers real time notifications over a live connection for events like publish decisions, mentions, budget thresholds, and expiring tokens. Quick popover Select the bell icon in the sidebar for a fast, unread only view: up to 5 items, with Mark as read on hover and Mark all as read / View all in the footer. Notifications Center Settings › Notifications shows every notification, read and unread, with search by message text, sortable Type and Date & Time columns, and bulk Mark as read , Mark as unread , and Delete actions. What triggers a notification | Event | What it means | | | | | Publish approved / rejected | Your published agent or skill version was reviewed. | | Mentioned or added to a conversation | A teammate @mentioned you or added you to a conversation. | | Index created, reindexed, or failed | A toolkit index finished or failed. | | Bucket expiration warning | Files in an artifact bucket will be deleted within 24 hours under its retention policy. | | Personal access token expiring | A token will stop working within 24 hours. | | Project or member budget threshold / limit reached | Shared model spend is near or at its monthly limit. | Several of these link straight to the relevant page — for example, an expiring token notification opens Settings › Personal Tokens, and a budget notification opens Settings › Usage. Troubleshooting Opening the popover does not mark items read automatically — use Mark as read or Mark all as read explicitly. Some links (for example, a mention) open the exact conversation and message; others open a settings page scoped to the relevant project. Personal tokens · Analytics and usage · Artifacts

title: Personal settings
text: Personal settings apply to you across every project — they never affect what your teammates see. Profile Settings › Profile shows your full name, email, user ID, and last login, and is where you sign out of Elitea. Preferences Settings › Preferences covers three areas: General — your theme: Dark, Light, or System. Voice personalization — your default text to speech voice, speed, and volume, with a preview button. Uses your project's configured server side voice model when available, otherwise your browser's built in voices. Sound notifications — whether Elitea plays a completion sound when a task finishes, and at what volume. AI Personality Settings › AI Personality sets the default communication style and any standing instructions applied to every new conversation you start. Default Personality — pick from Generic, QA, Nerdy, Quirky, Cynical, None (no personality overlay), or Bare (no Elitea identity at all, only your instructions). User Instructions — free text guidance (communication preferences, technical requirements, output format) that applies automatically to new conversations, agents, and pipelines. Settings save automatically as you edit; only new conversations pick up a change — existing ones keep what they started with. Start with the default persona and no instructions, use it for a few conversations, then adjust one setting at a time based on what you notice. Troubleshooting Confirm you are testing in a brand new conversation — existing conversations keep their original settings. Personality shapes tone and approach, not factual correctness — it is most visible in open ended or creative requests, not factual lookups. Memory · Chat

title: Personal tokens
text: A personal access token (PAT) authenticates API calls and IDE integrations as you, without using your password. Settings › Personal Tokens is where you create, inspect, and revoke them. Generate a token Select + . Give it a descriptive name and choose Never, or a number of days, weeks, hours, or minutes. The full token is shown only once — copy it immediately. It cannot be retrieved again after you close the dialog. Use "Never" only for personal development — set an expiration for anything used in a shared or production context. Manage tokens The table shows each token's last 4 characters value and an expiration status (a warning icon appears within 7 days of expiry). Select the preview icon to see ready made VS Code ( settings.json ) or JetBrains ( alita.xml ) configuration snippets for that token, copy or download them, or delete a token you no longer need. Troubleshooting It cannot be shown again — delete it and generate a new one. They only appear once a model configuration is selected and you are outside the Public project. Check whether its token expired; expired tokens stop authenticating immediately. Support Assistant · API and MCP endpoints

title: Project settings
text: Project settings cover the parts of a project every member shares: its identity, its background context, its secrets, and who belongs to it. General Settings › General shows the project's icon, name, and teammate count (hidden for the Public project), plus connection details for OpenAI compatible clients — an OpenAI BaseURL , server URL, and project ID you can copy for external tooling. A Default Modules section lets you turn modules (image creation, data analysis, planner, smart tools selection, swarm mode, and more) on or off by default for chats and agents project wide; members can still override the default per conversation. Project Context Project Context is a background document — up to 2,500 characters of Markdown — that Elitea applies silently to every AI interaction in the project: domain, terminology, workflows, and constraints the model should always know. It is visible only in the Public project. Select Create to write it manually, or Build with AI to generate a first draft from a plain language description. Use Edit with AI to describe a change and review a side by side diff before it saves. Turning Project Context off preserves its content — you can turn it back on later. Individual agents can opt out with Ignore Project Context in their Advanced settings. Secrets Settings › Secrets is the project's vault for sensitive values — passwords, tokens, API keys — that credentials and toolkits reference instead of storing plain text. Only Admin, System, or Editor roles can access this section. Create a secret with a unique name (letters, digits, underscores only) and a value; the name cannot change afterward. Hide removes a secret from the UI and from future selection, while credentials already using it keep working. Delete removes it permanently — any credential using it fails authentication immediately. Every mutation is applied under a row lock, so two people editing the same secret at once no longer clobber each other's change. Users Settings › Users lists project members with their role and last login; it is hidden for a personal project. Only Admin can invite, edit roles for, or remove members. Select + Invite users , enter one or more email addresses (comma separated), and pick one or more roles. Edit a single user's roles, or select several and batch edit them together. Delete a user individually or in a batch, with confirmation. Available roles are System, Admin, Editor, Viewer, and Monitor; a user can hold more than one. Troubleshooting It only appears in the Public project, and requires view permission. Your role does not include access — ask a project admin. Recreate the secret under the same name, or update the credential to a new one. AI Providers · Credentials · Agents

title: Settings overview
text: Select Settings in the sidebar to manage Elitea at two levels: project settings, which apply to everyone in the current project, and personal settings, which apply only to you across every project. Project settings General info, project context, secrets, and users. Models, embeddings, and AI credentials. Adoption, cost, and health metrics; budget consumption. Some project sections only appear in specific contexts: Project Context , Prompts , and Environment are visible only in the Public project; Users is hidden in a personal project; Analytics requires the analytics enabled admin flag and Usage requires cost budgets enabled . Personal settings Profile, preferences, and AI personality. Context window management for new conversations. API and IDE access tokens. Your notification history and preferences. Your role and permissions determine what you can view or edit within each section — some, like Secrets and Users, are restricted to Admin, System, or Editor roles. For definitions of roles and permissions, see the Glossary.

title: Skills
text: A skill is a focused, reusable instruction set — write it once in Markdown, attach it to as many agents as you need, and invoke it mid conversation with ~skill name . Skills are available in team and personal projects only; the Skills menu is hidden when the Public project is selected. Create a skill Select + in the sidebar, or Create from the Skills page, and choose Skill. Give it a Name (lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only, no leading/trailing hyphen, 64 characters max, and it must not contain "claude" or "anthropic"), a Description , and optional tags. Enter the skill's instructions in the Markdown editor, up to 5,000 characters. Toggle Edit/Preview to check formatting. The skill opens with a test chat panel on the right so you can verify its behavior before attaching it to any agent. Select Generate with AI in the General section to describe what the skill should do in plain language and get a drafted name, description, and instructions to review before saving. Test a skill The right hand test chat is ephemeral — it is not saved and clears when you leave the page. Pick a model and adjust its settings the same way you would in a normal conversation, including voice input and playback if configured for the project. Versions Skills keep a version history, the same base plus named versions model agents and pipelines use: Every new skill starts on the base version. Edit and save it as many times as you like. Click New version and give it a name. base is reserved and cannot be reused as a custom name; a duplicate name is rejected. Use the version dropdown next to the skill's name to switch versions. Saving always updates whichever version is currently selected. Set default pins a version as the one a new attachment to an agent proposes — it does not change what an agent that has already attached this skill uses; that stays fixed at attach time (see Attach a skill to an agent below). You cannot delete the default version or base , and a published version is frozen until you unpublish it. Compare versions opens a read only, side by side diff of the current version's instructions and tags against any other version — useful for checking what changed before you restore or publish. Restore copies a named version's instructions and tags back onto base , overwriting base 's current content. This is the skill equivalent of agents' "Set as default": skills have no separate "currently active" pointer to repoint, so restoring means writing the content directly onto the one version the unversioned editor and every new attachment read. Delete version removes any version except base , the current default, or a published one. Export, import, fork, and publish Export downloads the current version as a .md file; Import on the Skills page uploads one back (always as a new base version, regardless of the version it was exported from). Fork copies a skill version into a project you choose. Publish submits a version to Catalog; Unpublish removes it. See Skill publishing. Attach a skill to an agent Open the agent, scroll to its Skills section, and select + Skill to search and attach — up to five skills per agent version. Each attachment uses the skill's base version by default; select the version name on the card to switch. Attaching requires the agent to be saved first. Use a skill in chat In a conversation with an agent that has skills attached, type ~ to open a picker of that agent's skills, then select one to invoke its instructions for that turn. Delete a skill Deleting a skill removes it from every agent it is attached to. Confirm in the dialog — unlike the agent editor's delete confirmation, it does not ask you to type the skill's name. Troubleshooting You are in the Public project — switch to a team or personal project. Check the character limits and validation rules on Name, Description, and Instructions, and confirm something actually changed since the last save. Save the agent first, or check whether it already has five skills attached. The current agent has no skills attached yet — attach one and start a new conversation. Agents · Entity versioning · Import/export · Catalog

title: Toolkits
text: A toolkit is a configured integration with an external service, or with an Elitea native capability, that gives agents and pipelines the ability to act. Elitea serves 52 toolkit types; see the full toolkit catalogue for the list, categories, and which deployment worker runs each one. Create a toolkit Select + Toolkit from the Toolkits page, or /toolkits/create from anywhere. Choose a type from the categorized tile grid, or search by name. Give it a Name and Description , select or create a Credential , and set any type specific parameters. For index capable types, optionally select an embedding model to turn on indexing; indexes are kept in the platform's vector store, so there is no vector storage setting. In Tools , turn on only the operations the toolkit needs — grouped as Read, Create & update, Delete, and Execute — then Save . A type the agent worker cannot build is served with its tile greyed out and a reason, rather than shown broken or omitted ( 865). Check the toolkit catalogue for which types run. Advanced users can switch a toolkit's configuration to Raw JSON editing from the form/JSON toggle. Organize with folders The Folders panel on the right groups toolkits for easier navigation. Create a folder with + Folder , then move a toolkit into it from the folder icon on its card (hover to reveal it). Removing a toolkit from a folder does not delete it — it just returns to the main list. Pin frequently used folders from their three dot menu. Shared credentials in team projects If a toolkit uses a shared credential that each team member must supply individually, a Credential setup required banner appears on its card until you create the matching private credential. Changing a shared credential can make the toolkit stop working for teammates who have not configured their own — consider the impact before doing so. Test a toolkit Select Test on a toolkit's detail page to open a dedicated test view: pick a tool, a model, and any required parameters, then run it and review the result. See Test toolkit tools. Indexing Toolkit types that carry an index data tool (Artifact, the ADO family, Bitbucket, Confluence, Figma, GitHub, GitLab, Jira, QTest, SharePoint, TestRail, XRAY Cloud, and the Zephyr family) show an Indexes panel once an embedding model is configured and the Index data tool is turned on. Use it to create, reindex, or delete indexes. See Indexing overview. MCP servers MCP servers extend agents, pipelines, and conversations with tools from an external Model Context Protocol server, configured the same way as a toolkit. The MCPs menu is shown when your administrator has turned on MCP menu exposure. Remote MCP — an HTTP/HTTPS based server. Provide its URL and authentication (a bearer token, OAuth client credentials, or custom headers), then load and select its tools. Pre built MCP servers — administrator curated connections your project can enable directly. See Pre built MCP servers. A connection shows Connected or Disconnected on its card. Elitea's own MCP connections run over streamable HTTP only — there is no local, STDIO based MCP server or client in the platform. Enable Make tools available by MCP on a toolkit's Tools section to expose its selected tools to external MCP clients through Elitea's own MCP server. See Make tools available by MCP. Use toolkits and MCPs Attach a toolkit or MCP from an agent's or pipeline's Tools section, or add it as a participant directly in a conversation. Troubleshooting Verify the selected credential and any required URL or project identifier, and confirm the target service is reachable. The running worker may not support that type — check the toolkit catalogue, or ask your administrator whether the type is restricted for this project. Confirm the toolkit type supports indexing, that an embedding model is configured in AI Providers, and that Index data is turned on in Tools. For a Remote MCP, verify the server URL is reachable and its authentication has not expired. Credentials · How to use credentials · Webhooks and triggers · Toolkit catalogue

title: Pipeline node reference
text: The Flow editor's Add node menu offers more node types than the runtime compiler admits. This page lists both, plus the rules for node ids and state. Node types These are the only node types the pipeline compiler accepts and will actually run: decision · agent · toolkit · mcp · hitl · llm · printer · router · state modifier See the node type guides: interaction nodes, execution nodes, and control flow nodes (which also covers state modifier and printer, the utility nodes). tool , pipeline , function , loop , loop from tool , and condition still appear in some existing flows for backward compatibility, but the compiler has no execution arm for them — their editor tooltips still point at older migration material that this documentation set does not carry forward. Rebuild any flow that still uses one of these with an admitted node type instead. code and custom render in the editor but have no compiler arm either, so the Add node menu withholds them. END marks a pipeline's completion point; ghost and defaultType are internal placeholders you will not select directly. Node id rules A node id must match ^[A Za z0 9 .: ]+$ and be 128 bytes or fewer. Avoid spaces or other punctuation — a node id containing a space is a common cause of a pipeline that fails to save or compile. Reserved state keys Do not use these names for your own state variables — the runtime writes to them directly: elitea hitl resume v1 · elitea tool resume v1 · elitea llm tool resume v1 · elitea pipeline node event scope v1 · elitea pipeline result trace v1 · elitea application task v1 · elitea application messages v1 · elitea application result v1 · elitea subgraph result v1 · output · result · router output · elitea response · printer output · state types · context info · hitl decisions · hitl interrupt · parallel tasks · pipeline blocked · session id · thread id · execution finished · chat history input and messages are built into every pipeline (see State) but are not on the reserved list — you can still read them, just don't redefine them with a conflicting shape. Troubleshooting It is likely one of the render only/deprecated types. Replace it with the closest runtime admitted type — for example, replace tool with toolkit , and function with code 's admitted successor once available, or an llm / toolkit node. Check the id against the ^[A Za z0 9 .: ]+$ pattern and the 128 byte limit — spaces are the most common cause. Confirm its name is not one of the reserved keys above; pick a different name if it collides. Pipelines · Pipeline structure · Flow editor · YAML editor

title: Frequently asked questions
text: Your personal project is visible only to you — a sandbox for experimenting. A team project shares its agents, pipelines, toolkits, and conversations with every member, according to their role. Switch between them with the project selector at the top of the sidebar. Skills are hidden when the Public project is selected. Switch to a team or personal project. Only if the agent uses a toolkit that requires one. A plain agent with no toolkits needs only a model — configured once for the whole project in AI Providers. Yes, as long as they were saved as a version. Use the version dropdown on the agent to switch to an earlier version, or export a version as a backup file. It stops working immediately. Elitea shows the same "unavailable" message whether a link was revoked, expired, or never valid, so a recipient cannot tell which case applies. Its model likely hit the configured Max Completion Tokens limit. Increase it in the agent's model settings — and check any nested agents' limits too. See Troubleshooting. Yes — one credential can back several toolkits and agents. See Credentials. Which toolkit types are available depends on the worker your deployment runs, and on any restriction your administrator applied. See the toolkit catalogue. No — deleting a secret is permanent, and every credential referencing it fails authentication immediately. Consider hiding a secret first if you only want to stop new usage while confirming nothing still depends on it. See Troubleshooting for error message specific fixes, or reach your platform administrator through Help and support.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Start with the health checklist for a fast overall check, then use the category sections below for a specific error message. Quick health checklist Green dot on the Elitea logo = connected. Red = check your network. You can create the entities your role should allow (agents, toolkits, credentials). Test Connection on a credential returns success. Visible on a toolkit only once an embedding model and the Index data tool are both configured. If any of these fail, fix that first — most downstream errors trace back to one of them. Agent and LLM issues The model hit its Max Completion Tokens limit. Increase the value in the agent's model settings; check nested agents too if the issue appears mid chain. The message or instructions triggered the provider's safety mechanism. Avoid sensitive topics and phrasing that reads like a prompt injection attempt (for example, "ignore user input"); state the purpose of any such instruction clearly. Shared models on your deployment share per second/minute/day limits across every user. Wait and retry, or switch models. Input plus history exceeded the model's context window. Reduce the input, turn on context management, or index the source instead of pasting it directly. Turn on Structured Output when an LLM node has more than one output variable, and instruct the model to return JSON keyed by your variable names. Pipeline configuration issues Every pipeline needs one designated starting node — open the node's three dot menu and select Entry Point . A node (Agent, Decision, Router, and others) has an empty Task field — required fields must be filled before the pipeline can run. The task field must explicitly reference the variable, using an f string or the variable picker — listing a variable under Input alone does not pass it to the node automatically. A node has no agent or toolkit selected in its dropdown — select one. Toolkit and integration issues The connected account's token cannot see one or more items. Narrow the source with a filter (JQL for Jira, CQL for Confluence) and retry — items deleted mid run also surface this way. Recheck the credential's key or token for typos, extra whitespace, or expiry, and confirm the authentication method (basic vs. bearer) matches what the target service expects. Its configuration has a Limit field capping results per request — raise it in the toolkit's configuration. A required field is empty after an import or an update to the toolkit's schema — review every configuration section, including advanced settings, and fill anything marked required. MCP issues For a Remote MCP, verify the server URL is reachable and its authentication has not expired. Elitea's MCP connections are HTTP only — there is no local, STDIO based server or client to run first. Reload the MCP's configuration page, and confirm the server actually exposes tools once connected. Look at the end of the message for the real cause — one failure can cascade into another. For pipelines, the error usually names the node ("During task with name 'Agent1'"); open that node's configuration first. Operator checks Two different things answer "is the platform healthy," at two different levels. Infrastructure liveness and readiness elitea main exposes unauthenticated health endpoints for your load balancer, orchestrator, or uptime check: GET /healthz — liveness. Answers once the process is up; it does not check dependencies. GET /readyz — readiness. Checks the dependencies the service actually needs (for example, the database) and reports which one failed if it is not ready. Point your platform's health probe (Kubernetes liveness/readiness probe, or an external uptime monitor) at these rather than at an authenticated API route. The Health tab (application level) Inside the app, Settings › Analytics › Health (gated by the analytics enabled admin flag — see Features and configuration) reports on the LLM gateway path specifically: Error codes — a table of upstream and gateway error codes seen recently, by count. This reads the gateway's per request log, not the billing ledger, so a call that was refused by a budget, rejected by policy, or failed upstream shows up here even though it never generated a billed event. Model health — which configured models are currently returning errors, and how often. Activity trend — a day by day chart of request volume. If nothing appears on this tab, check the analytics enabled flag before assuming the platform is idle — the tab is gated off entirely rather than shown empty when the flag is off. Use the infrastructure endpoints to answer "is the service up," and the Health tab to answer "are calls through the LLM gateway succeeding." For upgrades, backups, scaling, and a fuller troubleshooting table for a Kubernetes deployment, see Day 2 operations. Check the FAQs, or reach your platform administrator through Help and support.

title: What's new
text: Elitea ships frequent, small releases. This page summarizes the most recent user visible changes; it is not a full changelog. Sign in is single sign on by default Deployments now sign people in through OIDC or SAML, with SCIM provisioning. The local username/password sign in is off unless an operator turns it on, and every local user now needs a real e mail address — none is invented from the login any more. Client deployment readiness You can now configure a fresh deployment entirely from the UI — set the first global administrators, create a project, and add an AI provider — without running SQL by hand. Platform parity wave A broad pass closed gaps across several areas at once: issue triage fixes, the toolkit catalogue, the support assistant bot, Inventory, and wiki source connections all received fixes and completions. Post release fixes Follow up fixes landed for session handling, admin 403 errors, invite links, the maintenance splash screen, voice configuration, artifact bucket access control lists, and the admin Tasks page. The secrets vault also gained write locking, so concurrent edits to the same secret no longer overwrite each other silently. Detailed release notes are published as GitHub releases on the platform repository. This page lists only the changes that affect what you see or do in the product.
